akhfash:3-3.t: He said: ﴿بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ﴾; he says ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ﴾ by Our revealing ﴿إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾. He made (ما) a noun for the action [i.e. a maṣdar-forming mā] and made (أَوْحَيْنا) its ṣila (relative clause).

akhfash:4-4.t:
He said: ﴿إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾: He repeated the verb, though one of the two could suffice. This follows the dialect of those who say "ضَرَبْتُ زَيْداً ضَرَبْتُهُ" (I struck Zayd, I struck him), and it is emphasis (tawkīd), like ﴿فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ كُـلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ﴾. Some read (أَحَدَ عْشَرَ) with the ʿayn quiescent, and likewise (تِسْعَةَ عْشَرَ) and so on up to twenty: since the noun was long and had many vowelled letters, they made it quiescent. They did not make it quiescent in their saying "اثْنَيْ عَشَر" and "اثْنَتا عَشْرَةَ" because of the quiescent letter before the ʿayn. The vowelling of the ʿayn in all of this is the original.
As for His words ﴿رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾: since He made them like rational beings in prostrating and obeying, He made them like humans in using the masculine when He gave them the plural, just as He said ﴿عُلِّمْنَا مَنطِقَ ٱلطَّيْرِ﴾. The poet said [in the khafīf metre, and it is the two hundred and thirty-third poetic witness]:
صَدَّها مَنْطِقُ الدَّجاجِ عَنِ القَصْدِ * وَضَرْبُ الناقُوسِ فَاجْتُنِبا
(The speech of the fowls and the striking of the church-bell turned her from her course, so both were avoided.)
And He said ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمْلُ ٱدْخُلُواْ مَسَاكِنَكُمْ﴾ since an ant spoke and so became like a rational being. And He said ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾: since He made them obey, He likened them to humans. Like that is ﴿قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ﴾ by this analogy, except that it is masculine while not being masculine, just as some feminines are made masculine. Some people said He said ﴿طائِعين﴾ only because the two came together with what is in them, so some imagined it "masculine"; or it may be as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning its people. And as you say "صَلى المَسْجِدُ" (the mosque prayed) meaning the people of the mosque, except that you construe the verb according to the latter [the omitted word], as they said: "اِجْتَمَعتْ أَهُلُ اليمامَةِ" (the people of al-Yamāma gathered). And He said ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ ٱللَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ لاَ تَسْجُدُواْ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلاَ لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾, because a group of non-humans is feminine. Someone said it means "لِلَّذِي خَلَقَ الآياتِ" (to the One who created the signs), and I do not think he said that except out of ignorance of Arabic. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the two hundred and thirty-fourth poetic witness]:
إِذْ أَشْرَفَ الديكُ يَدْعُوا بَعْضَ أُسْرَتِهِ * إِلى الصِياحِ وَهُمْ قُوْمٌ مُعَازِيلٌ
(When the cock rose up, calling some of his family to crow, and they are a people unarmed.)
So he made the fowls "a people" by the latitude of the language. Another said, meaning the wolf [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and thirty-second poetic witness]:
وَأَنْتَ امْرُؤٌ تَعْدُو عَلى كُلِّ غِرَّةٍ * فَتُخْطِىءُ فِيها مَرَّةً وَتَصِيُبُ
(You are a man who pounces on every unguarded moment, sometimes missing and sometimes hitting the mark.)
And another said [in the rajaz metre, and it is the two hundred and thirty-fifth poetic witness]:
فَصَبَّحَتْ وَالطَّيْرُ لَمْ تَكَلَّمِ * جابِيَةً طُمَّتْ بِسَيْلٍ مُفعَم
(She came at dawn, while the birds had not yet spoken, to a cistern brimming with a full torrent.)

akhfash:5-5.t: He said: ﴿فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيْداً﴾, i.e. "so that they contrive a plot for you". It is not like ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾. He wanted to join the verb to it with the lām, as it is joined with "إلى" (to), as you say "قَدَّمْتُ لَهُ طَعاماً" (I set food before him), meaning "قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْهِ". And He said ﴿يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ﴾; like it is ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ﴾. If you wish, ﴿فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيْداً﴾ may have the meaning "فَيَكِيدوك" (so they plot against you), and you make the lām like ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾; and His words ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾ are only "لِمَكانِ رَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُون" (they fear on account of their Lord).

akhfash:9-9.t: He said: ﴿أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضاً يَخْلُ لَكُمْ﴾. "الأَرْضُ" (land) here is not an adverb (ẓarf); rather "في" (in) has been omitted from it and then the verb made to govern it, as you say "تَوَجَّهْتُ مَكَّةَ" (I headed Mecca).

akhfash:14-14.t: He said: ﴿وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾. "العُصْبَةُ" and "العِصابَةُ" are a group that has no singular, like "القَوْم" (people) and "الرَّهْط" (band).

akhfash:18-18.t: He said: ﴿بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ﴾: He made "the blood" a "lie" because a lie was told about it, as you say "الليلةُ الهِلالُ" (tonight is the new moon) with the nominative, and as He said ﴿فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِّجَارَتُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:19-19.t: He said: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُواْ وَارِدَهُمْ﴾: He used the masculine after the feminine because "السَيَّارة" (the caravan) in meaning refers to men.

akhfash:23-23.t: He said: ﴿مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُ رَبِّيۤ﴾, i.e. "I seek refuge in Allah, a seeking of refuge". He made it a substitute for pronouncing the verb, because it is a maṣdar, even though [the verb is] not in use, like "سُبْحانَ". Some say "مَعاذَةَ اللهِ", and say "ما أَحْسَنَ مَعْناةَ هَذا الكلامِ" (how fine is the meaning of this speech), meaning "المعنى".

akhfash:24-24.t: He said: ﴿وَهَمَّ بِهَا﴾: he did not intend the indecency, but something short of it which does not sever [his] standing as one of Allah's friends (al-walāya).

akhfash:25-25.t: He said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾; he says "except prison or a painful punishment", because the light "أنْ" together with what it governs is a noun with the status of "السّجْن" (prison).

akhfash:32-32.t: He said: ﴿وَلَيَكُوناً مِّن ٱلصَّاغِرِينَ﴾: the pause on it is (وَلِيَكُونا), because when what precedes the light nūn (of emphasis) has fatḥa and you pause on it, you make it a quiescent alif, like your saying "رَأَيْتُ زيدا". Like it is ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾: the pause on it is "لَنَسْفَعا".

akhfash:35-35.t: He said: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ ٱلآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ﴾: he put the nūn (of emphasis) in this position because this is a position in which "أيّ" (which?) occurs; since the interrogative particle can enter here, the nūn entered it, because the nūn occurs in questions. You say "بدا لَهُم أَيُّهُم يأخذون" (it occurred to them which of them they would take), i.e. it became clear to them.

akhfash:44-44.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلأَحْلاَمِ بِعَالِمِينَ﴾: with one of the two bāʾs he joined the verb to the noun, and the other entered because of "ما" — and it is the latter.

akhfash:45-45.t: He said: ﴿وَٱذَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾. It is "اِفْتَعَل" from "ذُكَرْتُ", so its origin is "اِذْتَكَر"; but the two [dhāl and tāʾ] came together in one word with close points of articulation, and they wanted to assimilate. The first is a voiced (majhūr) letter, and the first is merged only into the second, while the second is voiceless (mahmūs); they disliked that its voicing should be lost, so in place of the tāʾ they put a voiced letter from its own place of articulation, namely the dāl, because the letter before it is voiced. They did not use ṭāʾ because ṭāʾ, besides being voiced, is velarised (muṭbaq). Some said (مُذّكِر), changing the tāʾ into dhāl and then merging the dhāl into it. And this verse has been read ﴿أَن يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحاً﴾, and it is "أَنْ يَفْتَعِلا" from "الصُلْح": the tāʾ came after the ṣād, and the ṣād was not merged into it because of its voicing and velarisation, so they changed the tāʾ into ṣād [يَصَّالَحا]. [Translator's note: the quoted reading «يُصْلِحَا» is the one with no tāʾ; the discussion concerns the readings «يَصَّالَحَا/يَصَّلِحَا» and «يَصْطَلِحَا»; translated as written.] Some read (يَصْطَلِحا), and it is the good one: since the ṣād could not be assimilated into the tāʾ, a velarised letter was put in place of the tāʾ.

akhfash:51-51.t: He said: ﴿إِذْ رَاوَدتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِ﴾. Some of the people of knowledge said: "They [the women] solicited him, not the king's wife [alone]". It is also permissible, even if it was one woman, to say "راوَدْتُنَّ" (you [fem. pl.] solicited), just as you say (إِنَّ الناسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُم), where this is one person here: by His words "لَكُمْ" He means the Prophet — Allah bless him — and by (الناسَ) "Abū Sufyān", according to what they mentioned.

akhfash:76-76.t: He said: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ﴾, using the feminine, and He said ﴿وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ﴾, because there He meant "الصُّواع" (the measuring cup), and "الصُّواع" is masculine — though some make "الصّواع" feminine — and here He meant "السِّقَايَةَ" (the drinking cup), which is feminine. They are two names for one thing, like "الثَّوْبُ" and "المِلْحَفَةُ" (garment, wrap): masculine and feminine for one thing.

akhfash:80-80.t:
He said: ﴿خَلَصُواْ نَجِيّاً﴾: He made "النَجِيَّ" (confidant) apply to a group, like your saying "هُمْ لِي صديق" (they are a friend to me).
And He said ﴿قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ﴾: they claimed that he was the greatest of them in intelligence, not in age.

akhfash:83-83.t: He said ﴿عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَنِي بِهِمْ جَمِيعاً﴾ only because he meant the one who stayed behind, together with the two, and he was the greatest of them in intelligence.

akhfash:84-84.t: He said: ﴿يَٰأَسَفَىٰ عَلَى يُوسُفَ﴾: when you pause, you add hāʾ at its end, because it is like the alif of lamentation (alif al-nudba).

akhfash:85-85.t: He said: ﴿تَالله تَفْتَؤُاْ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ﴾. They claimed that (تَفْتَأُ) means "تَزَالُ" (you continue); that is why the oath fell on it, as though they said: "By Allah, you do not cease remembering Yūsuf".

akhfash:92-92.t: He said: ﴿لاَ تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾: (اليومَ) is a pause; then he began anew and said ﴿يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾, praying for forgiveness for them as a new sentence.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّي لَيَحْزُنُنِي أَنْ تَذْهَبُوا﴾ i.e. your going ﴿بِهِ﴾ because of being parted from him ﴿وَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَأْكُلَهُ الذِّئْبُ﴾ what is meant by it is the genus (the wolf as a kind), and their land had many wolves ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ غَافِلُونَ﴾ occupied (with other things).

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَئِنْ﴾ a lām of oath ﴿أَكَلَهُ الذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾ a group ﴿إِنَّا إِذًا لَخَاسِرُونَ﴾ incapable. So he sent him with them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا بِهِ وَأَجْمَعُوا﴾ they resolved ﴿أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ فِي غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ﴾ The jawāb (answer) of لَمَّا is omitted, i.e. "they did that": they stripped off his shirt after beating him, humiliating him and intending to kill him, and lowered him down; when he reached the middle of the well they dropped him so that he would die. He fell into the water, then took refuge on a rock. They called to him and he answered them, thinking they would have mercy on him, and they wanted to crush him with a rock, but Yahūdhā (Judah) prevented them. ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ﴾ in the well, a true revelation, when he was seventeen years old or younger, to reassure his heart: ﴿لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾ after this day ﴿بِأَمْرِهِمْ﴾ of their deed ﴿هَذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ who you are at the time of the informing.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَاءُوا أَبَاهُمْ عِشَاءً﴾ at the time of evening ﴿يَبْكُونَ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ﴾ shooting (in a contest) ﴿وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِنْدَ مَتَاعِنَا﴾ our clothes ﴿فَأَكَلَهُ الذِّئْبُ وَمَا أَنْتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ﴾ believing ﴿لَنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ﴾ in your view: you would suspect us in this story out of love for Yūsuf, so how (would you believe us) when you already think ill of us?

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَجَاءُوا عَلَى قَمِيصِهِ﴾ its position is accusative (naṣb) as an adverbial of place (ẓarfiyya), i.e. on top of it ﴿بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ﴾ i.e. possessing falsehood (false blood): they had slaughtered a young goat, smeared it (the shirt) with its blood, and forgot to tear it, and they said, "It is his blood." ﴿قَالَ﴾ Yaʿqūb, when he saw it intact and knew their lie: ﴿بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ﴾ made seem attractive ﴿لَكُمْ أَنْفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا﴾ which you then did to him ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾ in which there is no anguish; it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "my course is …" ﴿وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ﴾ the One from whom help is sought ﴿عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ﴾ you relate concerning the matter of Yūsuf.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ﴾ travellers from Madyan to Egypt, who halted near Yūsuf's well ﴿فَأَرْسَلُوا وَارِدَهُمْ﴾ the one who goes down to the water to draw from it ﴿فَأَدْلَى﴾ he let down ﴿دَلْوَهُ﴾ into the well; Yūsuf clung to it and he drew him out, and when he saw him ﴿قَالَ يَا بُشْرَايَ﴾ in one reading [بُشْرَى]; calling out to it is figurative, i.e. "Come, for this is your time!" ﴿هَذَا غُلَامٌ﴾ His brothers learned of it and came to him ﴿وَأَسَرُّوهُ﴾ i.e. they concealed his affair, making him ﴿بِضَاعَةً﴾ by saying, "This is our slave who ran away," and Yūsuf kept silent out of fear that they would kill him. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ﴾ they sold him to them ﴿بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ﴾ deficient ﴿دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾ twenty or twenty-two ﴿وَكَانُوا﴾ i.e. his brothers ﴿فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِينَ﴾ Then the caravan brought him to Egypt, and the one who had bought him sold him for twenty dinars, a pair of sandals and two garments.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِي اشْتَرَاهُ مِنْ مِصْرَ﴾ he was Qiṭfīr, the ʿAzīz ﴿لِامْرَأَتِهِ﴾ Zulaykhā ﴿أَكْرِمِي مَثْوَاهُ﴾ his abode with us ﴿عَسَى أَنْ يَنْفَعَنَا أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا﴾ and he was impotent. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We saved him from being killed and from the well, and inclined the heart of the ʿAzīz towards him, ﴿مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt, until he attained what he attained ﴿وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ﴾ the interpretation of dreams; it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to something implied (muqaddar) attached to (mutaʿalliq) مَكَّنَّا, i.e. "so that We might give him dominion", or the wāw is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَى أَمْرِهِ﴾ Exalted is He; nothing can thwart Him ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are the disbelievers ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ﴾ which is thirty years, or thirty-three ﴿آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْمًا﴾ wisdom ﴿وَعِلْمًا﴾ understanding of the religion, before he was sent as a prophet ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We rewarded him ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ to themselves.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَرَاوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا﴾ she was Zulaykhā ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ i.e. she sought from him that he lie with her ﴿وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوَابَ﴾ of the house ﴿وَقَالَتْ﴾ to him ﴿هَيْتَ لَكَ﴾ i.e. "Come!", and the lām is for clarification (tabyīn); in one reading with a kasra on the hāʾ, and in another with a ḍamma on the tāʾ. ﴿قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ﴾ I seek refuge with Allah from that ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ the one who bought me ﴿رَبِّي﴾ my master ﴿أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَايَ﴾ my abode, so I will not betray him concerning his wife ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) ﴿لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ the fornicators.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ﴾ she intended intercourse with him ﴿وَهَمَّ بِهَا﴾ he intended that ﴿لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās said: Yaʿqūb was made to appear to him and struck him on the chest, and his desire went out through his fingertips. The jawāb (answer) of لَوْلَا is "he would have lain with her". ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ We showed him the proof ﴿لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ﴾ betrayal ﴿وَالْفَحْشَاءَ﴾ fornication ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا الْمُخْلِصِينَ﴾ in obedience; and in one reading with a fatḥa on the lām [الْمُخْلَصِينَ], i.e. the chosen ones.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ﴾ Yūsuf hastened to it in order to flee, and she in order to hold on to him, so she seized his garment and pulled him towards her ﴿وَقَدَّتْ﴾ she tore ﴿قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا﴾ they found ﴿سَيِّدَهَا﴾ her husband ﴿لَدَى الْبَابِ﴾ So she declared herself innocent, then ﴿قَالَتْ مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءًا﴾ fornication ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يُسْجَنَ﴾ be confined, i.e. imprisonment ﴿أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, by his being beaten.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Yūsuf, declaring his innocence: ﴿هِيَ رَاوَدَتْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِي وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا﴾ her cousin (her paternal uncle's son); it is related that he was in the cradle, and he said: ﴿إِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ﴾ the front ﴿فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ﴾ behind ﴿فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَى﴾ her husband ﴿قَمِيصَهُ قُدَّ مِنْ دُبُرٍ قَالَ إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. your saying {مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ} etc. ﴿مِنْ كَيْدِكُنَّ﴾ O women ﴿إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌ﴾ Then he said: O

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا﴾ matter, and do not mention it, so that it does not spread ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرِي﴾ O Zulaykhā ﴿لِذَنْبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنْتِ مِنَ الْخَاطِئِينَ﴾ the sinners. And the news became known and spread.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ the city of Egypt ﴿امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ تُرَاوِدُ فَتَاهَا﴾ her slave ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا﴾ a tamyīz (specification), i.e. love of him has entered the shighāf of her heart, i.e. its covering ﴿إِنَّا لَنَرَاهَا فِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ i.e. in error ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, through her love for him.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ﴾ their backbiting of her ﴿أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ﴾ she prepared ﴿لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً﴾ food cut with a knife, for reclining while eating it, namely citron ﴿وَآتَتْ﴾ she gave ﴿كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ﴾ to Yūsuf ﴿اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُ أَكْبَرْنَهُ﴾ they regarded him as great ﴿وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾ with the knives, and they did not feel the pain because their hearts were occupied with Yūsuf ﴿وَقُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ﴾ declaring Him transcendent ﴿مَا هَذَا﴾ i.e. Yūsuf ﴿بَشَرًا إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ because of the beauty he possessed, which is not usually found in a human being; and in the hadith: "that he was given half of beauty".

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿قَالَتْ﴾ the wife of the ʿAzīz, when she saw what had befallen them: ﴿فَذَلِكُنَّ﴾ so this is he ﴿الَّذِي لُمْتُنَّنِي فِيهِ﴾ concerning love of him; an explanation of her excuse ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ فَاسْتَعْصَمَ﴾ he refused ﴿وَلَئِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ مَا آمُرُهُ﴾ to do ﴿لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًا مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ﴾ the abased. Then they said to him, "Obey your mistress."

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ﴾ I will incline ﴿إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ﴾ I will become ﴿مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾ the sinners. What is intended by this is supplication; that is why Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ his supplication ﴿فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of speech ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of deeds.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا﴾ it appeared ﴿لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الْآيَاتِ﴾ which indicated Yūsuf's innocence, that they should imprison him; this is indicated by ﴿لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّى﴾ until ﴿حِينٍ﴾ in which people's talk would cease. So he was imprisoned.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ﴾ two servants of the king, one of them his cupbearer and the other in charge of his food. They saw him interpreting dreams and said, "Let us test him." ﴿قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا﴾ he was the cupbearer ﴿إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا﴾ i.e. grapes ﴿وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ﴾ he was the one in charge of the food ﴿إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا﴾ inform us ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ of its interpretation ﴿إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them, informing them that he knew the interpretation of dreams: ﴿لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِ﴾ in your sleep ﴿إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ in waking life ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمَا﴾ its interpretation ﴿ذَلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي﴾ in it is an urging of them to believe; then he strengthened it with his words ﴿إِنِّي تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ﴾ the religion ﴿قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿كَافِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ آبَائِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ﴾ it is fitting ﴿لَنَا أَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ because of our being protected (from sin) ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the affirmation of Oneness (tawḥīd) ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are the disbelievers ﴿لَا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Allah, and so they associate partners. Then he made his call to them to believe explicit, saying:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿يَا صَاحِبَيِ﴾ O two inmates of ﴿السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ﴾ better? A question of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr).

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا﴾ with which you named idols ﴿أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا﴾ for worshipping them ﴿مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ argument and proof ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿الْحُكْمُ﴾ the decree ﴿إِلَّا لِلَّهِ﴾ alone ﴿أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذَلِكَ﴾ the affirmation of Oneness ﴿الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ﴾ the straight ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are the disbelievers ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the punishment they are heading towards, and so they associate partners.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا﴾ i.e. the cupbearer, he will come out after three days ﴿فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ﴾ his master ﴿خَمْرًا﴾ as was his custom ﴿وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ﴾ he will come out after three days ﴿فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ﴾ This is the interpretation of your dreams. They said, "We did not see anything," and he said: ﴿قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ﴾ which you asked about, whether you told the truth or lied.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ﴾ was certain ﴿أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا﴾ he was the cupbearer ﴿اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ your master, and say to him: "In the prison there is a young man imprisoned unjustly." Then he came out. ﴿فَأَنْسَاهُ﴾ i.e. the cupbearer ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ﴾ Yūsuf before ﴿رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ﴾ Yūsuf remained ﴿فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ﴾ it is said seven, and it is said twelve.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ﴾ the king of Egypt, al-Rayyān ibn al-Walīd ﴿إِنِّي أَرَى﴾ i.e. I saw ﴿سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ﴾ swallowing them ﴿سَبْعٌ﴾ cows ﴿عِجَافٌ﴾ plural of عَجْفَاء (lean) ﴿وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ﴾ i.e. seven ears ﴿يَابِسَاتٍ﴾ which had twined around the green ones and overcome them ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُؤْيَايَ﴾ explain its interpretation to me ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾ then interpret it for me.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ these are ﴿أَضْغَاثُ﴾ jumbles of ﴿أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا﴾ i.e. of the two young men, and he was the cupbearer ﴿وَادَّكَرَ﴾ in it the original tāʾ is changed into a dāl and assimilated into the dāl, i.e. تَذَكَّرَ (he remembered) ﴿بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾ a while, the state of Yūsuf ﴿أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ﴾ So they sent him, and he came to Yūsuf and said: O

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ﴾ the one abundant in truthfulness ﴿أَفْتِنَا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ لَعَلِّي أَرْجِعُ إِلَى النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the king and his companions ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ its interpretation.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ﴾ i.e. sow ﴿سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا﴾ consecutively; this is the interpretation of the seven fat ones ﴿فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ﴾ i.e. leave it ﴿فِي سُنْبُلِهِ﴾ so that it does not spoil ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ which you should thresh.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the seven fertile ones ﴿سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ﴾ barren, hard; this is the interpretation of the seven lean ones ﴿يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ﴾ of the grain sown in the fertile years, i.e. you will eat it in them ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the seven barren ones ﴿عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ﴾ with rain ﴿وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ﴾ grapes and other things, because of its fertility.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ﴾ when the messenger came to him and informed him of its interpretation ﴿ائْتُونِي بِهِ﴾ i.e. the one who interpreted it ﴿فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ﴾ i.e. Yūsuf ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ and asked him to come out ﴿قَالَ﴾ intending to make his innocence manifest ﴿ارْجِعْ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَاسْأَلْهُ﴾ to ask ﴿مَا بَالُ﴾ what is the state of ﴿النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّي﴾ my master ﴿بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ﴾ So he went back and informed the king, and he gathered them.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ﴾ your affair ﴿إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ did you find in him any inclination towards you? ﴿قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ الْآنَ حَصْحَصَ﴾ has become clear ﴿الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in his saying {هِيَ رَاوَدَتْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِي}. Yūsuf was informed of that, and he said:

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the seeking of exoneration ﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ the ʿAzīz ﴿أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ﴾ concerning his wife ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:53-53.t: Then he humbled himself before Allah and said: ﴿وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي﴾ from slips ﴿إِنَّ النَّفْسَ﴾ the genus ﴿لَأَمَّارَةٌ﴾ much given to commanding ﴿بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا﴾ in the sense of مَنْ (whom) ﴿رَحِمَ رَبِّي﴾ and so protected him ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي﴾ I will make him exclusively mine, with no partner. So the messenger came to him and said, "Answer the king." He rose, bade farewell to the people of the prison and prayed for them, then washed, put on fine clothes and went in to him. ﴿فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ﴾ to him ﴿إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ﴾ possessing standing and trust over our affairs. "So what do you think we should do?" He said, "Gather food, and sow abundant crops in these fertile years, and store the food in its ears; then people will come to you to get provisions from you." He said, "And who will take charge of this for me?"

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Yūsuf ﴿اجْعَلْنِي عَلَى خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt ﴿إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ possessing safekeeping and knowledge of its affairs; and it is said: a scribe and accountant.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ like Our favour to him in delivering him from prison ﴿مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Egypt ﴿يَتَبَوَّأُ﴾ settling ﴿مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ﴾ after the straitness and confinement. In the story it is related that the king crowned him, gave him his signet ring, appointed him in the place of the ʿAzīz and dismissed the latter; he died afterwards, and the king married him to his wife, whom he found to be a virgin, and she bore him two sons. He established justice in Egypt and people submitted to him. ﴿نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ﴾ than the reward of this world ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ﴾ The years of drought set in and struck the land of Canaan and Syria.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَجَاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ﴾ except Binyāmīn, to obtain provisions, since it had reached them that the ʿAzīz of Egypt was giving out food for its price ﴿فَدَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ﴾ that they were his brothers ﴿وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ they did not recognise him, because of the long time since they had seen him and their thinking that he had perished. They spoke to him in Hebrew, and he said, as if disapproving of them, "What has brought you to my land?" They said, "For provisions." He said, "Perhaps you are spies." They said, "Allah forbid!" He said, "Then where are you from?" They said, "From the land of Canaan, and our father is Yaʿqūb, the Prophet of Allah." He said, "And does he have children other than you?" They said, "Yes; we were twelve. Our youngest went away and perished in the wilderness, and he was the dearest of us to him; his full brother remained, and he kept him back to console himself with him for the loss of him." So he ordered that they be lodged and honoured.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ﴾ he gave them their full measure ﴿قَالَ ائْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَبِيكُمْ﴾ i.e. Binyāmīn, so that I may know your truthfulness in what you said ﴿أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّي أُوفِي الْكَيْلَ﴾ I give it in full without diminishing ﴿وَأَنَا خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي﴾ i.e. provisions ﴿وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ﴾ a prohibition, or conjoined to the position of فَلَا كَيْلَ, i.e. "you will be deprived and will not come near".

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالُوا سَنُرَاوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ﴾ we will strive to ask him of him ﴿وَإِنَّا لَفَاعِلُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَتِهِ﴾ and in one reading [لِفِتْيَانِهِ], his servants ﴿اجْعَلُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ﴾ which they had brought as the price of the provisions, and it was dirhams ﴿فِي رِحَالِهِمْ﴾ their containers ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ﴾ and emptied their containers ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ to us, because they would not consider it lawful to keep it.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ﴾ if you do not send our brother to him ﴿فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ ﴿وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿قَالَ هَلْ﴾ not ﴿آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ﴾ Yūsuf ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ and you did to him what you did ﴿فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حِفْظًا﴾ and in one reading [حَافِظًا]; a tamyīz (specification), like their saying "لِلَّهِ دَرُّهُ فَارِسًا" (how excellent he is as a horseman!) ﴿وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾ so I hope that He will grant His protection of him.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي﴾ مَا is interrogative, i.e. what more of the king's generosity could we seek than this? It has also been read with the tāʾ (two dots above), as an address to Yaʿqūb, and they had told him about his generosity to them. ﴿هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا﴾ we will bring them provisions (mīra), which is food ﴿وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ﴾ for our brother ﴿ذَلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ﴾ easy for the king, because of his generosity.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّى تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا﴾ a covenant ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ by your swearing ﴿لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ﴾ by your dying or being overpowered so that you are unable to bring him. They agreed to that. ﴿فَلَمَّا آتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ﴾ to that effect ﴿قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ﴾ we and you ﴿وَكِيلٌ﴾ witness. And he sent him with them.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَقَالَ يَا بَنِيَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا﴾ Egypt ﴿مِنْ بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَادْخُلُوا مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ﴾ so that the evil eye does not strike you ﴿وَمَا أُغْنِي﴾ I avert ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ by saying that ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ﴾ a connective (ṣila) ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ which He has decreed for you; that is only out of compassion ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ﴾ alone ﴿عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ in Him I have trusted ﴿وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ﴾ Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. separately ﴿مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. His decree ﴿مِنْ﴾ a connective (ṣila) ﴿شَيْءٍ إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا﴾ which was the wish to ward off the evil eye, out of compassion ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ﴾ because of Our teaching him ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are the disbelievers ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ Allah's inspiration of His chosen ones.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَى يُوسُفَ آوَى﴾ he drew ﴿إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ إِنِّي أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ﴾ do not grieve ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of envy towards us. He told him not to inform them, and agreed with him that he would devise a stratagem to keep him with him.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ﴾ it was a measuring vessel (ṣāʿ) of gold studded with gems ﴿فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ﴾ Binyāmīn ﴿ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ﴾ a crier called out, after they had left Yūsuf's assembly ﴿أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ﴾ the caravan ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالُوا وَ﴾ having ﴿أَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ مَاذَا﴾ what is it that ﴿تَفْقِدُونَ﴾ (it) [Translator's note: the gloss adds only the pronoun هُ, i.e. "what is it that you are missing"].

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿قَالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ﴾ the measuring vessel (ṣāʿ) of ﴿الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ﴾ of food ﴿وَأَنَا بِهِ﴾ the load ﴿زَعِيمٌ﴾ guarantor.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ﴾ an oath containing the sense of wonder ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ﴾ we have never stolen.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. the crier and his companions ﴿فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ﴾ i.e. of the thief ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ﴾ in your saying "we are not thieves", and it is found among you?

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ﴾ he is to be enslaved; then it is emphasised by his saying ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ i.e. the thief ﴿جَزَاؤُهُ﴾ i.e. of the stolen thing, nothing else; and this was the custom of the family of Yaʿqūb ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ the recompense ﴿نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ by theft. So they declared openly to Yūsuf that their containers might be searched.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ﴾ and searched them ﴿قَبْلَ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ﴾ so that he would not be suspected ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَهَا﴾ i.e. the drinking-cup ﴿مِنْ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ﴾ Allah the Exalted said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ stratagem ﴿كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ﴾ We taught him the stratagem for taking his brother ﴿مَا كَانَ﴾ Yūsuf ﴿لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ﴾ as a slave for theft ﴿فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ﴾ the law of the king of Egypt, because its penalty was beating and a fine of twice the value of what was stolen, not enslavement ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ his taking him by his father's law; i.e. he was unable to take him except by the will of Allah, by His inspiring him to ask his brothers and their answering according to their custom ﴿نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتِ مَنْ نَشَاءُ﴾ with the genitive construct (iḍāfa) and with tanwīn [دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ], in knowledge, like Yūsuf ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ﴾ among created beings ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ more knowledgeable than him, until it ends with Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿قَالُوا إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. Yūsuf: he had stolen from his maternal grandfather an idol of gold and broken it so that he would not worship it ﴿فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا﴾ did not show it ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ The pronoun refers to the statement in his words: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to himself ﴿أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا﴾ than Yūsuf and his brother, because of your stealing your brother from your father and wronging him ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ knowing ﴿بِمَا تَصِفُونَ﴾ you relate concerning him.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا﴾ who loves him more than us and is consoled by him for his son who perished, and parting from him will grieve him ﴿فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا﴾ enslave him ﴿مَكَانَهُ﴾ in his stead ﴿إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ in your actions.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ﴾ accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose verb has been omitted and which is annexed to its object, i.e. "we seek refuge with Allah from" ﴿أَنْ نَأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا مَتَاعَنَا عِنْدَهُ﴾ He did not say "whoever stole", guarding against falsehood. ﴿إِنَّا إِذًا﴾ if we took someone else ﴿لَظَالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْأَسُوا﴾ they despaired ﴿مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا﴾ they withdrew ﴿نَجِيًّا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) that serves for one and for more than one, i.e. conferring privately with one another ﴿قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ﴾ in age, Rūbīl, or in judgement, Yahūdhā ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَوْثِقًا﴾ a covenant ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ concerning your brother ﴿وَمِنْ قَبْلُ مَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿فَرَّطْتُمْ فِي يُوسُفَ﴾ and it is said that مَا is maṣdariyya (infinitival), a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is مِنْ قَبْلُ ﴿فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ﴾ I will leave ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ the land of Egypt ﴿حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أَبِي﴾ to return to him ﴿أَوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي﴾ with the release of my brother ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ﴾ the most just of them.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿ارْجِعُوا إِلَى أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا يَا أَبَانَا إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَا﴾ against him ﴿إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا﴾ with certainty, from seeing the measuring vessel in his saddlebag ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ﴾ what was hidden from us when we gave the covenant ﴿حَافِظِينَ﴾ Had we known that he would steal, we would not have taken him.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيهَا﴾ it is Egypt, i.e. send to its people and ask them ﴿وَالْعِيرَ﴾ i.e. the people of the caravan ﴿الَّتِي أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا﴾ and they were people of Canaan ﴿وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ﴾ in what we say. So they returned to him and said that to him.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ﴾ made seem attractive ﴿لَكُمْ أَنْفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا﴾ which you then did; he suspected them because of what they had done before in the matter of Yūsuf ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾ is my patience ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَنِي بِهِمْ﴾ Yūsuf and his two brothers ﴿جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of my state ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His doing.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَتَوَلَّى عَنْهُمْ﴾ ceasing to speak to them ﴿وَقَالَ يَا أَسَفَى﴾ the alif replaces the yāʾ of the possessive (yāʾ al-iḍāfa), i.e. "O my grief" ﴿عَلَى يُوسُفَ وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ﴾ their blackness was effaced and changed to whiteness from his weeping ﴿مِنَ الْحُزْنِ﴾ over him ﴿فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾ grieved and distressed, not showing his distress.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ﴾ not ﴿تَفْتَأُ﴾ will you cease ﴿تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّى تَكُونَ حَرَضًا﴾ on the verge of perishing because of the length of your illness; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in which one and more than one are alike ﴿أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْهَالِكِينَ﴾ the dead.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them ﴿إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي﴾ it is intense grief that cannot be borne patiently until it is poured out (yubathth) to people ﴿وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ not to anyone else, for He is the One to whom complaint is of benefit ﴿وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that Yūsuf's dream is true and that he is alive.

celaleyn:87-87.t: Then he said: ﴿يَا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ﴾ seek news of them ﴿وَلَا تَيْأَسُوا﴾ do not despair ﴿مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ﴾ His mercy ﴿إِنَّهُ لَا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ So they set off towards Egypt, to Yūsuf.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا الضُّرُّ﴾ hunger ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَاعَةٍ مُزْجَاةٍ﴾ rejected, everyone who sees it rejects it because of its poor quality; it was counterfeit dirhams, or something else ﴿فَأَوْفِ﴾ give in full ﴿لَنَا الْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَا﴾ by overlooking the poor quality of our goods ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ﴾ rewards them. He softened towards them, was overcome by compassion, and lifted the veil between himself and them; then

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them, in rebuke: ﴿هَلْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ بِيُوسُفَ﴾ of beating, selling and so on ﴿وَأَخِيهِ﴾ of your mistreating him after his brother was parted from him ﴿إِذْ أَنْتُمْ جَاهِلُونَ﴾ of what Yūsuf's affair would lead to.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ after they recognised him, when his features became apparent, seeking to make sure: ﴿أَإِنَّكَ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between them in both ways ﴿لَأَنْتَ يُوسُفُ قَالَ أَنَا يُوسُفُ وَهَذَا أَخِي قَدْ مَنَّ﴾ has bestowed favour ﴿اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا﴾ by bringing us together ﴿إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّقِ﴾ fears Allah ﴿وَيَصْبِرْ﴾ in what befalls him ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ In it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ﴾ has preferred you ﴿اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا﴾ with kingship and other things ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. إِنَّا ﴿كُنَّا لَخَاطِئِينَ﴾ sinful in your matter, for we humiliated you.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ﴾ reproach ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ﴾ he mentioned it specifically because it is the likeliest occasion for reproach, so other days are all the more so (free of it) ﴿يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾ He asked them about his father, and they said, "His eyesight has gone," so he said:

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿اذْهَبُوا بِقَمِيصِي هَذَا﴾ it was the shirt of Ibrāhīm which he wore when he was thrown into the fire; it was around his (Yūsuf's) neck in the well, and it is from Paradise. Jibrīl told him to send it and said, "It has the scent of Paradise in it, and it is not cast upon any afflicted person without his being healed." ﴿فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَى وَجْهِ أَبِي يَأْتِ﴾ he will become ﴿بَصِيرًا وَأْتُونِي بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ الْعِيرُ﴾ departed from ʿArīsh of Egypt ﴿قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ﴾ to those of his sons and their children who were present ﴿إِنِّي لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ﴾ the east wind (ṣabā) brought it to him, by the leave of Allah the Exalted, from a distance of three days' journey, or eight, or more ﴿لَوْلَا أَنْ تُفَنِّدُونِ﴾ you would call me foolish; (otherwise) you would believe me.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to him ﴿تَاللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِي ضَلَالِكَ﴾ your error ﴿الْقَدِيمِ﴾ of your excessive love for him and your hope of meeting him despite the long time that has passed.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿جَاءَ الْبَشِيرُ﴾ Yahūdhā, with the shirt; he had carried the blood-stained shirt, so he wanted to gladden him as he had grieved him ﴿أَلْقَاهُ﴾ he cast the shirt ﴿عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فَارْتَدَّ﴾ became again ﴿بَصِيرًا قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا اسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا خَاطِئِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ He postponed that until the pre-dawn (saḥar), so that it would be nearer to being answered, or until the night before Friday. Then they set out for Egypt, and Yūsuf and the notables went out to meet them.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَى يُوسُفَ﴾ in his tent ﴿آوَى﴾ he drew ﴿إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ﴾ his father and his mother, or his maternal aunt ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ to them ﴿ادْخُلُوا مِصْرَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ﴾ So they entered, and Yūsuf sat on his throne.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ﴾ he seated them with him ﴿عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ the throne ﴿وَخَرُّوا﴾ i.e. his parents and his brothers ﴿لَهُ سُجَّدًا﴾ a prostration of bowing, not of placing the forehead (on the ground); it was their greeting in that age ﴿وَقَالَ يَا أَبَتِ هَذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُؤْيَايَ مِنْ قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقًّا وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي﴾ to me ﴿إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ السِّجْنِ﴾ he did not say "from the well", out of graciousness, so that his brothers would not be ashamed ﴿وَجَاءَ بِكُمْ مِنَ الْبَدْوِ﴾ the desert ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ نَزَغَ﴾ sowed discord ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِمَا يَشَاءُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of His creation ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His doing. His father stayed with him twenty-four years, or seventeen years; the period of his separation had been eighteen, or forty, or eighty years. Death came to him, and he enjoined Yūsuf to carry him and bury him beside his father; so he went himself and buried him there, then returned to Egypt and lived after him twenty-three years. When his affair was complete and he knew that it would not last, his soul yearned for the everlasting kingdom, and he said:

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ﴾ the interpretation of dreams ﴿فَاطِرَ﴾ Creator of ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي﴾ the One who takes charge of my interests ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ﴾ of my forefathers. He lived after that a week or more and died aged one hundred and twenty. The Egyptians vied with one another over his grave, so they placed him in a chest of marble and buried him in the upper Nile so that the blessing would reach both its banks. So glory be to Him whose kingdom has no end!

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned of the matter of Yūsuf ﴿مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ﴾ the reports of ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ what was hidden from you, O Muḥammad ﴿نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ with Yūsuf's brothers ﴿إِذْ أَجْمَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ﴾ in plotting against him, i.e. they resolved upon it ﴿وَهُمْ يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ against him; i.e. you were not present with them so as to know their story and tell it; rather, knowledge of it came to you only by way of revelation.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿وَمَا أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ﴾ for their faith ﴿بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَمَا تَسْأَلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿مِنْ أَجْرٍ﴾ which you would take ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هُوَ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾ how many ﴿مِنْ آيَةٍ﴾ indicating the Oneness of Allah ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ they see them ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ they do not reflect on them.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ inasmuch as they acknowledge that He is the Creator and Provider ﴿إِلَّا وَهُمْ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him, by worshipping idols. That is why they used to say in their talbiya: "Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns," meaning them (the idols).

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿أَفَأَمِنُوا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَاشِيَةٌ﴾ a retribution that envelops them ﴿مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾ suddenly ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ the time of its coming.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي﴾ and he explained it by his words ﴿أَدْعُو إِلَى﴾ the religion of ﴿اللَّهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ﴾ clear proof ﴿أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي﴾ believed in me; conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أَنَا, the mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is what precedes it ﴿وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ﴾ declaring Him transcendent above partners ﴿وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ also part of His way.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا يُوحَى﴾ and in one reading with nūn and a kasra on the ḥāʾ [نُوحِي] ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ not angels ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرَى﴾ the cities, because they are more knowledgeable and more forbearing, unlike the people of the desert, because of their coarseness and ignorance ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا﴾ the people of Mecca ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ i.e. the end of their affair, their destruction for denying their messengers ﴿وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. Paradise ﴿خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ Allah ﴿أَفَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْقِلُونَ], i.e. "do you not understand this, O people of Mecca, and so believe?"

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ marks the limit of what is indicated by {وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا}, i.e. their help was delayed until ﴿إِذَا اسْتَيْأَسَ﴾ despaired ﴿الرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوا﴾ the messengers were certain ﴿أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِّبُوا﴾ with shadda: a denial after which there would be no belief; and with the light form [كُذِبُوا], i.e. the nations thought that the messengers had failed to keep the promise of help they had been given ﴿جَاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُنَجِّي﴾ with two nūns, with shadda and without, and with one nūn, with shadda, as a past verb [فَنُجِّيَ] ﴿مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا﴾ Our punishment ﴿عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ the polytheists.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ﴾ i.e. of the messengers ﴿عِبْرَةٌ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ people of understanding ﴿مَا كَانَ﴾ this Quran ﴿حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَى﴾ fabricated ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ it was ﴿تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ before it, of the scriptures ﴿وَتَفْصِيلَ﴾ the explanation of ﴿كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ needed in the religion ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ they are mentioned specifically because they benefit from it, unlike others.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الر﴾ Allah knows best what He means. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ these ayahs ﴿آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran — and the annexation is in the sense of مِنْ ("of") — ﴿الْمُبِينِ﴾ which makes the truth distinct from falsehood.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ in the language of the Arabs ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ may understand its meanings.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا﴾ by Our revealing ﴿إِلَيْكَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. وَإِنَّهُ ("and indeed [the matter is]") ﴿كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ﴾. Mention

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ﴾ Jacob: ﴿يَا أَبَتِ﴾ with kasra, indicating an omitted alif that was converted from the yāʾ [of the first-person possessive]; ﴿إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ﴾ in a dream ﴿أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿لِي سَاجِدِينَ﴾ — it is pluralised with yāʾ and nūn because of the description with prostration, which is one of the attributes of rational beings.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيْدًا﴾ scheme to destroy you out of envy, since they know its interpretation: that they are the stars, the sun is your mother and the moon your father. ﴿إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ manifest in enmity.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ as you saw ﴿يَجْتَبِيكَ﴾ will choose you ﴿رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ﴾ the interpretation of dreams ﴿وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ﴾ with prophethood ﴿وَعَلَى آلِ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ his children, ﴿كَمَا أَتَمَّهَا﴾ with prophethood ﴿عَلَى أَبَوَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His dealing with them.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي﴾ the story of ﴿يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ﴾ — and they were eleven — ﴿آيَاتٌ﴾ lessons ﴿لِلسَّائِلِينَ﴾ about their story. Mention

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا﴾ i.e. some of Joseph's brothers to others: ﴿لَيُوسُفُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿وَأَخُوهُ﴾ his full brother Benjamin ﴿أَحَبُّ﴾ khabar (predicate) ﴿إِلَى أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ﴾ a group. ﴿إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ﴾ error ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ clear, in preferring the two of them over us.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿اقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ أَوِ اطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا﴾ i.e. in a distant land; ﴿يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ﴾ in that he will turn to you and not pay attention to anyone else; ﴿وَتَكُونُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ i.e. after killing Joseph or casting him away ﴿قَوْمًا صَالِحِينَ﴾ by repenting.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿قَالَ قَائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ — he was Judah —: ﴿لَا تَقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ﴾ cast him ﴿فِي غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ﴾ the dark depth of the well — and in one reading in the plural — ﴿يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السَّيَّارَةِ﴾ the travellers, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ﴾ what you intended of separating [him from his father]. So they contented themselves with that.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَنَّا عَلَى يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَنَاصِحُونَ﴾ looking after his interests.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا﴾ to the open country ﴿نَرْتَعْ وَنَلْعَبْ﴾ with nūn and yāʾ in both [يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ] — we will be lively and enjoy ourselves freely; ﴿وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾.

daas-irab:33-35.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿السِّجْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَحَبُّ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحب. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ مِن a preposition and ما a relative; the two are attached to أحب. ﴿يَدْعُونَنِي﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural; the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil, the [second] nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to يدعونني. ﴿وَإِلَّا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, إن is conditional and لا is negating. ﴿تَصْرِفْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its fāʿil latent. ﴿عَنِّي﴾ the two are attached to تصرف. ﴿كَيْدَهُنَّ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct) and the nūn is the sign of the feminine plural; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿أَصْبُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined with fāʾ. ﴿إِلَيْهِنَّ﴾ the two are attached to أصب. ﴿وَأَكُنْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, conjoined to what precedes and jussive like it; its noun (ism) is omitted. ﴿مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to استجاب; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَصَرَفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction (ʿāṭifa), and a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to صرف. ﴿كَيْدَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi and the nūn is the sign of the feminine plural; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ إنّ, and the hāʾ is its noun; هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and السميع and العليم are its two khabars. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿بَدا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif owing to impossibility (al-taʿadhdhur). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to بدا. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the two are attached to بدا. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). ﴿رَأَوُا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; ما and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of a genitive (jarr) as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath; يسجننه is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is its mafʿūl, and the omitted wāw of the group is its fāʿil; the clause is the fāʿil of بدا. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of jarr. ﴿حِينٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) by حتى; the two are attached to يسجننه.

daas-irab:36-37.t: ﴿وَدَخَلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) دخل; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿السِّجْنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), placed first. ﴿فَتَيانِ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif because it is a dual; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿قالَ أَحَدُهُما﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). [Translator's note: the source calls the same clause both conjoined and resumptive; translated as written.] ﴿إِنِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun (ism). ﴿أَرانِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility (al-taʿadhdhur); the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya) and the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi of أراني. ﴿وَقالَ الْآخَرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنِّي أَرانِي﴾ إنّ and its noun; the clause أراني, whose i'rab has already been given, is the khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَحْمِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to أحمل. ﴿رَأْسِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خُبْزاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of خبز. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to تأكل or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نَبِّئْنا﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to نبئنا. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ إنّ and its noun. ﴿نَراكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied on the alif owing to impossibility; the kāf is its mafʿūl and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached to نراك. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا يَأْتِيكُما طَعامٌ﴾ لا is negating; يأتيكما is an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ owing to heaviness (al-thiqal), and the kāf is its mafʿūl placed first. ﴿طَعامٌ﴾ fāʿil placed after; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿تُرْزَقانِهِ﴾ an imperfect verb, passive (mabnī lil-majhūl), nominative by the retention of the nūn; the alif is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is an adjective of طعام. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿نَبَّأْتُكُما﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil, the kāf its mafʿūl, and the mīm and alif are for the dual; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to نبأتكما. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to نبأتكما. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle governing the accusative (nāṣiba). ﴿يَأْتِيكُما﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the kāf is its mafʿūl and its fāʿil is latent; أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ذلِكُما﴾ ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance, the kāf for address, and the mīm and alif for the dual. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ مِن a preposition and ما a relative; the two are attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي﴾ a past verb; the nūn is for protection and the yāʾ is its mafʿūl placed first; ربي is the fāʿil and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَرَكْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِلَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ لا is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is an adjective of قوم. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to يؤمنون. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ the two are attached to كافرون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:38-39.t: ﴿وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿آبائِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ badal (substitute) for آبائي. ﴿وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ conjoined to إبراهيم. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَنا﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle governing the accusative (nāṣiba). ﴿نُشْرِكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), its fāʿil latent (mustatir); أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of a nominative as the noun (ism) of كان. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ; the two are attached to نشرك. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾid) preposition. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), genitive in form and accusative in position. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to فضل. ﴿وَعَلَى النَّاسِ﴾ conjoined to علينا. ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكنّ and its noun. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَشْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لكنّ. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿صاحِبَيِ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the yāʾ because it is a dual; the nūn was dropped for the annexation; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿السِّجْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَأَرْبابٌ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُتَفَرِّقُونَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿أَمِ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, conjoined to أرباب. ﴿الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ﴾ two adjectives of الله.

daas-irab:40-41.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَسْماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سَمَّيْتُمُوها﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent), the wāw is for vowel-lengthening (al-ishbāʿ), and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of أسماء. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) for the fāʿil of سميتموها, in the position of a nominative like it. ﴿وَآباؤُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to the tāʾ; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿بِها﴾ the two are attached to أنزل; the clause is a second adjective of أسماء. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾid) preposition. ﴿سُلْطانٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, genitive in form and accusative in position. ﴿إِنِ﴾ a particle of negation. ﴿الْحُكْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the two are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمَرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿إِنِ﴾ a particle governing the accusative (nāṣiba). [Translator's note: the Quranic text here is أَلَّا (أن + لا); the source prints ﴿إِنِ﴾ but parses it as the accusative-governing أن.] ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تَعْبُدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; and the wāw is [its] fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ﴾ إلا is a particle of restriction, and إياه is a detached pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, and أن and what follows it are in the position of a genitive by the omitted bāʾ; the two are attached to أمر. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿الدِّينُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْقَيِّمُ﴾ an adjective. ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لكنّ and its noun (ism). ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿صاحِبَيِ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the yāʾ because it is a dual; the nūn was dropped for the annexation; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿السِّجْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَمَّا﴾ a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl). ﴿أَحَدُكُما﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَيَسْقِي﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to أمّا, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness (al-thiqal), its fāʿil latent. ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَمْراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾ a particle of detailing and condition. ﴿الْآخَرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَيُصْلَبُ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response to أمّا, and an imperfect passive verb (mabnī lil-majhūl); its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted; the clause is the khabar. [Translator's note: in standard parsing the nāʾib fāʿil here is a latent pronoun (mustatir); the source says "omitted" (maḥdhūf).] ﴿فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ رَأْسِهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ﴾ a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective of الأمر. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to تستفتيان. ﴿تَسْتَفْتِيانِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:42-43.t: ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِلَّذِي﴾ a relative noun; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قال. ﴿ظَنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ أنّ and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of ظنّ. ﴿ناجٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of أنّ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the omitted yāʾ because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ the two are attached to ناج. ﴿اذْكُرْنِي﴾ an imperative verb; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān); the two are attached to اذكرني. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَنْساهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif owing to impossibility (al-taʿadhdhur); the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl, placed first. ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ fāʿil placed after. ﴿ذِكْرَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَلَبِثَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿فِي السِّجْنِ﴾ the two are attached to لبث. ﴿بِضْعَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to لبث. ﴿سِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is treated like a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun (ism); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿أَرى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied on the alif owing to impossibility, its fāʿil latent. ﴿سَبْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَقَراتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the khabar of إني. ﴿سِمانٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿يَأْكُلُهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl placed first. ﴿سَبْعَ﴾ fāʿil placed after. ﴿عِجافٌ﴾ an adjective; the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi of أرى. ﴿وَسَبْعَ﴾ conjoined to the earlier سبع. ﴿سُنْبُلاتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خُضْرٍ﴾ an adjective of سنبلات. ﴿وَأُخَرَ﴾ conjoined to سبع; it is genitive by the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). [Translator's note: the source says conjoined to سبع yet genitive; the genitive fits conjunction to سنبلات.] ﴿يابِساتٍ﴾ an adjective of أخر. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ أيّ is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), in the position of an accusative by the vocative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention (al-tanbīh). ﴿الْمَلَأُ﴾ badal (substitute) for أيّ, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ﴿أَفْتُونِي﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the nūn is for protection and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause and what precedes it are the object of the saying. ﴿فِي رُءْيايَ﴾ the two are attached to أفتوني, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لِلرُّءْيا﴾ the lām is a preposition and الرؤيا a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra implied on the alif owing to impossibility; the two are attached to تعبرون. ﴿تَعْبُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:44-46.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿أَضْغاثُ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هي أضغاث"; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَحْلامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negating, operating like ليس. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ the noun (ism) of ما. ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) عالمين. ﴿الْأَحْلامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِعالِمِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and عالمين is its khabar, genitive in form and nominative in position; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِي﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَجا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility (al-taʿadhdhur), its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْهُما﴾ the two are attached to نجا. ﴿وَادَّكَرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, conjoined to نجا. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to ادكر. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿أُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb; the kāf is its mafʿūl (object) and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِتَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to أنبئكم, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَرْسِلُونِ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the omitted first-person yāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يُوسُفُ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun, with an omitted vocative particle; it is indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of an accusative, and its clause has no grammatical position. ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾ أيّ is the one addressed with an omitted vocative particle; it is indeclinable on ḍamma because it is an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), in the position of an accusative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention (al-tanbīh). ﴿الصِّدِّيقُ﴾ badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); its clause has no grammatical position. ﴿أَفْتِنا﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl, its fāʿil latent. ﴿فِي سَبْعِ﴾ the two are attached to أفتنا. ﴿بَقَراتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿سِمانٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of بقرات. ﴿يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يابِساتٍ﴾ their i'rab has been given just above. ﴿لَعَلِّي﴾ لعلّ and its noun; the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) with no grammatical position. ﴿أَرْجِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿إِلَى النَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to أرجع. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعلّ and its noun; the mīm is for the masculine plural; the clause is a causal explanation with no grammatical position. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعلهم.

daas-irab:47-49.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿تَزْرَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿سَبْعَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) تزرعون. ﴿سِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is treated like a sound masculine plural. ﴿دَأَباً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and ما is a conditional noun governing the jussive, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. ﴿حَصَدْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿فَذَرُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿فِي سُنْبُلِهِ﴾ the two are attached to ذروه; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by إلا, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿مِمَّا﴾ مِن a preposition and ما a relative in the position of a genitive; the two are attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of قليلا. ﴿تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness (al-thiqal). ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the two are attached to يأتي. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿سَبْعٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿شِدادٌ﴾ an adjective. ﴿يَأْكُلْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural; the nūn is the fāʿil; the clause is a second adjective of سبع. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قَدَّمْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ the two are attached to قدمتم. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ excepted by إلا, accusative. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ مِن a preposition and ما a relative; the two are attached to an omitted adjective of قليلا. ﴿تُحْصِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ﴾ its i'rab has been given just above. ﴿عامٌ﴾ the fāʿil of يأتي. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to يغاث. ﴿يُغاثُ النَّاسُ﴾ an imperfect passive verb (mabnī lil-majhūl) and nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is an adjective of عام. ﴿وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يعصرون. ﴿يَعْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:50-51.t: ﴿وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what preceded. ﴿ائْتُونِي﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لمّا is temporal (ḥīniyya, "when"), attached to جاءه. ﴿جاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ﴾ a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi placed first and a fāʿil placed after; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿قالَ ارْجِعْ إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ the clause ارجع, made up of the imperative verb and its implicit (muḍmar) fāʿil, is the object of the saying. ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb ارجع. ﴿فَسْئَلْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its implicit fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to the clause ارجع. ﴿ما بالُ﴾ ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and بال is its khabar (predicate). ﴿النِّسْوَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّاتِي﴾ a relative noun in the position of a genitive as an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿قَطَّعْنَ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural; the nūn is the fāʿil. ﴿أَيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي﴾ إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, ربي is its noun (ism), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِكَيْدِهِنَّ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿قالَ ما خَطْبُكُنَّ﴾ ما is interrogative, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and خطبكن is khabar. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to خطبكن. ﴿راوَدْتُنَّ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and its fāʿil. ﴿يُوسُفَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ the two are attached to راودتن. ﴿قُلْنَ﴾ a past verb, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil. ﴿حاشَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the two are attached to حاشا. ﴿ما عَلِمْنا﴾ ما is negating, and علمنا is a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to علمنا. ﴿مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ مِن is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and سوء is genitive in form, accusative in position, as mafʿūl bihi of علمنا. ﴿قالَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿الْآنَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to حصحص. ﴿حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿راوَدْتُهُ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar. ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ the two are attached to راودته. ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إنّ [and] its noun. ﴿لَمِنَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and a preposition. ﴿الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ a genitive noun; the two are attached to the khabar.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ the lām is causal (lil-taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the causal lām; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنِّي﴾ أنّ and its noun (ism), standing in place of the two objects of يعلم. ﴿لَمْ أَخُنْهُ﴾ the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لا يَهْدِي﴾ the clause is the khabar. ﴿كَيْدَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْخائِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ.
