Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From your saying «اتَّكَأْنا عند فلان», 'we ate,' by way of metonymy, because from «دَعَوْتَه ليَطْعَمَ عندك» ('you invited him to eat with you'): you provided for him a cushion to recline on. Jamīl said:

2771 - فَظَلِلْنا بنعمةٍ واتَّكَأْنا ... وشَرِبْنا الحَلالَ مِنْ قُلَلِهْ
(We spent the day in comfort and reclined, and drank what is lawful from its jars.)"

End of quotation. I say: his saying «وشَرِبْنا» supports the meaning of «اتَّكَأْنا» as "we ate."

Abū Jaʿfar and al-Zuhrī read «مُتَّكَا» with doubled tāʾ and no hamza, and there are two aspects in it. The first: that its origin is «مُتَّكَأ» as the majority's reading, and its hamza was only lightened, as they say «تَوَضَّيْتُ» for «تَوَضَّأْتُ», so it became on the pattern of «مُتَّقَى». The second: that it is «مُفْتَعَل» from «أَوْكَيْتُ القِرْبة», when you tie its mouth with the thong, so the meaning is: "she prepared something that they could support themselves upon, either by reclining or by cutting with the knife"; and this second analysis is Abū l-Fatḥ's.

Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Hurmuz read «مُتَّكاءً» with doubling and lengthening; it is like the majority's reading except that he prolonged the fatḥa so that an alif arose from it, like his saying:

2772 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ومِنْ ذَمِّ الرجالِ بمنتزاحِ
(... and far from the blame of men.)

and his saying:

2773 - يَنْباع مِنْ ذفرى غَضُوبٍ جَسْرَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(It gushes from behind the ear of an angry, bold she-camel...)

and his saying:

2774 - أَعوذُ باللَّه مِنَ العَقْرابِ ... الشَّائِلاتِ عُقَدَ الأَذْنابِ
(I seek refuge with Allah from the scorpions that raise the knots of their tails.)

that is, «بمنتزح», «يَنْبَع» and «العقرب الشائلة».

Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Jaḥdarī and Abān ibn Taghlib read «مُتْكَاً» with ḍamma on the mīm, sukūn on the tāʾ and tanwīn on the kāf; likewise read Ibn Hurmuz, ʿAbd Allāh and Muʿādh, except that those two put fatḥa on the mīm. «المُتْكُ», with ḍamma and with fatḥa, is the citron, and it is said «الأُتْرُنْجُ»; they are two dialects, and they recited:

2775 - فَأَهْدَتْ مُتْكَةً لبني أبيها ... تَخُبُّ بها العَثَمْثَمَةُ الوَقاحُ
(She sent a citron to her father's sons, borne at a trot by the strong, hardy camel.)

It was said: rather it is a name for everything that is cut with a knife, such as citron and other fruits, and they recited:

2776 - نَشْرَبُ الإِثمَ بالصُّواعِ جِهاراً ... وترى المُتْكَ بيننا مُسْتعارا
(We drink wine openly from the goblet, and you see the «متك» circulating among us as a loan.)

It was said: it is from «مَتَك» in the sense of «بَتَك الشيءَ», that is, he cut it; on this, the mīm may be a substitute for the bāʾ, which is a regular substitution in the dialect of some people; and it is possible that it is from another root coinciding with this one. It was said: with ḍamma it is pure honey according to al-Khalīl, and the citron according to al-Aṣmaʿī. Abū ʿAmr reported the three forms for it, I mean ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the mīm; he said: it is the pure drink.

Al-Mufaḍḍal said: with ḍamma it is the table, or wine in the dialect of Kinda.

And His saying: {لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً}: either he intends one reclining-place for each woman, as His saying indicates: {وَآتَتْ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً}, or he intends the genus.

«السِّكِّين» is masculine and feminine; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said so, and al-Aṣmaʿī denied its feminine use. «السَّكِينة» is of the pattern «فَعِيلة» from «السكون». Al-Rāghib said: "It is so called because it removes the movement of the slaughtered animal."

His saying: {أَكْبَرْنَهُ}: the apparent view is that the hāʾ is the pronoun of Yūsuf. The meaning of «أَكْبَرْنَه» is: they magnified him and were stunned by his beauty. It was said: it is the hāʾ of pause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was said: «أَكْبَرْنَ» means «حِضْنَ» ('they menstruated') and the hāʾ is for pause; it is said «أَكْبَرَتِ المرأةُ» when she menstruates, and its reality is: she entered into maturity, because by menstruation she goes out of the limit of youth into maturity; and it is as if Abū l-Ṭayyib took from this explanation his saying:

2777 - خَفِ اللَّهَ واسْتُرْ ذا الجمالَ ببُرْقُعٍ ... فإنْ لُحْتَ حاضَتْ في الخُدورِ العواتِقُ
(Fear Allah and cover this beauty with a veil, for if you appear, the maidens in their chambers will menstruate.)"

End of quotation. That the hāʾ is for pause is refuted by the ḍamma on the hāʾ; had it been for pause it would be sākin. It may be said that he treated it like the hāʾ of the pronoun and treated continuation as pause in retaining it. Al-Shaykh said: "The consensus of the readers on ḍamma for the hāʾ in continuation is evidence that it is not the hāʾ of pause; for if it were the hāʾ of pause and a case of treating continuation as pause, the hāʾ would not be given ḍamma." I say: the hāʾ of pause is vowelled with the vowel of the pronoun hāʾ, treating it as such, and I have verified this in al-Anʿām; and they said the same about al-Mutanabbī's saying:

2778 - واحَرَّ قلباه مِمِّنْ قَلْبُه شَبِمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Oh, the burning of my heart, for the sake of one whose heart is cold...)

since it was related with ḍamma on the hāʾ in «قلباه», and they made it the hāʾ of pause. It is possible that «أَكْبَرْنَ» means «حِضْنَ» and the hāʾ is not for pause, but made the pronoun of the maṣdar indicated by its verb, that is, «أَكْبَرْنَ الإِكبار». They recited, to show that «الإِكبار» means menstruation, the saying:

2779 - يأتي النساءَ على أَطْهارِهِنَّ ولا ... يأتي النساءَ إذا أَكْبَرْن إكبارا
(He comes to women during their periods of purity, and does not come to women when they menstruate.)

Al-Ṭabarī said: "The verse is fabricated."

His saying: {حَاشَ للَّهِ}: the grammarians counted «حاشى» among the particles that waver between being a particle and a verb: if it governs the genitive it is a particle, and if it governs the accusative it is a verb; and it is among the particles of exception. Sībawayh did not recognize its verbal status, though others did, and they related from the Arabs: «غَفَر اللَّه لي ولِمنْ سمع دعائي حاشى الشيطانَ وابنَ الأصبغ», in the accusative, and they recited:

2780 - حشى رَهْطَ النبيِّ فإنَّ منهمْ ... بُحوراً لا تكدِّرُها الدِّلاءُ
(Except the clan of the Prophet, for among them are seas that buckets do not muddy.)

with «رَهْط» in the accusative. And «حشى» is a variant of «حاشى», as will come. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«حاشى» is a word that gives the sense of exoneration in the section of exception; you say «أساءَ القومُ حاشى زيدٍ» ('the people did wrong, except Zayd'). He said:

2781 - حاشى أبي ثوبانَ إنَّ بهِ ... ضِنَّاً عنِ المَلْحاة والشَّتْم
(Except Abū Thawbān, for he is too miserly for reproach and abuse.)

It is a particle among the particles of the genitive, placed in the position of exoneration and clearing; so the meaning of «حاشى اللَّهِ» is: the clearing of Allah and the exoneration of Allah, and it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd." Al-Shaykh said: "What he mentioned, that it gives exoneration in the section of exception, is unknown to the grammarians; there is no difference between your saying «قام القومُ إلا زيداً» and «قام القوم حاشى زيدٍ». When he gave the example «أساء القومُ حاشى زيدٍ» and understood from this example the clearing of Zayd from wrongdoing, he made that derived from it in every place. As for what he recited, «حاشا أبي ثوبان», this is how Ibn ʿAṭiyya and most grammarians recite it, but it is a verse in which they put the first half of one verse on the second half of another, in error, from two verses, which are:

2782 - حاشى أبي ثَوْبان إنَّ أبا ... ثَوْبانَ ليس ببُكْمَةٍ فَدْمِ
عمرَو بنَ عبدِ اللَّه إنَّ به ... ضِنَّاً عن المَلْحاةِ والشَّتْمِ
(Except Abū Thawbān — for Abū Thawbān is not a dumb, sluggish dolt — ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, for he is too miserly for reproach and abuse.)"

I say: his saying that the meaning mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī is unknown to the grammarians — they did not deny it; they simply did not mention it in their books, because most of their craft is in the making of the expressions rather than the meanings. When they mentioned «ليس», «لا يكون» and «غير» among the particles of exception, they did not mention their meanings, since their purpose was their equality with «إلا» in excluding, and that does not prevent an added meaning in those particles.

Al-Mubarrad and others, like Ibn ʿAṭiyya, claimed that its verbal status is definite when a preposition follows it, as in the noble verse. They said: because a preposition does not enter upon its like except for emphasis, as in his saying:

2783 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا لِلِما بهم أبداً دواءُ
(... and for what afflicts them there is never a remedy.)

and the saying of another:

2784 - فأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْأَلْنني عن بما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they came to be asking me no more about what is in him...)

so it is definitely a verb, its agent being the pronoun of Yūsuf, that is, «حاشى يوسف», and «للَّه» is a preposition and genitive noun attached to the verb before it, the lām giving cause, that is, "Yūsuf kept far from committing what she accused him of, out of obedience to Allah and his standing with Him, or because of Allah's raising him above being accused of what she accused him of"; that is, he avoided disobedience for the sake of Allah.

People answered that by saying that «حاشى» in the noble verse is neither a particle nor a verb; rather it is a noun of a maṣdar, a substitute for the utterance of its verb, as if it were said "exoneration for Allah and clearing for Him," and it was not given tanwīn only out of regard for its origin from which it was transferred, namely the particle. Do you not see that they said «مِنْ عن يمينه», making «عن» a noun without declining it, and they said «مِنْ عليه», not retaining its alif with the pronoun, but leaving «عن» on its building, and turning the alif of «على» with the pronoun, out of regard for its origin? So answered al-Zamakhsharī, and al-Shaykh followed him without ascribing the answer to him. There is something to consider in it.

As for his saying "out of regard for its origin," it implies that it was transferred from particle status to noun status, and that happens only in the case of proper names, meaning that they name a person with a particle, and they have two doctrines about that: declension, and quotation (ḥikāya). That they transfer a particle to a noun, that is, make it a noun, is unknown. As for his citing «عن» and «على», it does not help him, because «عن», in the state of being a noun, is built only because of its resemblance to the particle in being set on two letters, not because it remains on its building. As for the turning of the alif of «على» with the pronoun, there is no indication in it, because we know this in what is of established noun status by agreement, like «لدى».

It is better to say: what appears in the answer to the majority's reading is that it is an accusative noun, as set out above, and the reading of Abū l-Simāl «حاشاً للَّه» in the accusative indicates it; only that they turned the tanwīn into alif as they turn it in pause, then treated continuation as pause, as they did in many places, some of which have been given and the like of which will come to you.

It was said in answer to that: rather «حاشا» was built, in its noun state, because of its resemblance to «حاشا» in its particle state in wording and meaning, as «عن» and «على» were built, for the reason we mentioned.

Some of them said: the lām is redundant. This is very weak; its place is poetry. Al-Mubarrad and his followers cited as evidence for its verbal status the occurrence of its imperfect. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:

2785 - ولا أرى فاعِلاً في الناسِ يُشْبِهُهُ ... ولا أُحاشي من الأقوامِ مِنْ أَحَدِ
(And I see no doer among people who resembles him, and I exempt from the peoples no one.)

They said: the word's inflection from past to imperfect is definitely evidence of its verbal status. The majority answered that by saying that this is taken from the wording of the particle, as they said «سَوَّفْتُ بزيد» and «لَوْلَيْت له», that is, "I said to him: I will do (sawfa)" and "I said to him: if it were (law), if it were"; and this is of that kind, and it is possible.

Among those who preferred the verbal side was Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī; he said: "«حاش» in His saying «حاش للَّه» cannot be other than either the genitive particle in exception, or a verb on the pattern «فاعَل»; it cannot be the genitive particle because it does not enter upon its like, and because particles are not subject to omission unless they have doubling; so it is established that it is «فاعَل» from «الحشا», which means the side; the meaning is that he became in a «حَشاً», that is, in a side; and the agent of «حاش» is «يوسف», and the implied form is: 'he kept far from this matter, for Allah,' that is, for fear of Him.'"

His saying "a preposition does not enter upon its like" is granted, but it is not a preposition here, as was set out above. His saying "nothing is dropped from a particle except when it is doubled" is disputed, and what indicates it is their saying «مُنْ» for «منذ» when it governs the genitive, dropping its ʿayn, with no doubling. They said: what indicates that its origin is «منذ» with nūn is its diminutive «مُنَيْذ», and this is established in its chapter.

Abū ʿAmr alone read «حاشى» with two alifs: an alif after the ḥāʾ and an alif after the shīn, in the two occurrences of this sūra in continuation, and dropping it in pause, following the script, as we shall point out. The others drop the last alif in continuation and pause. As for Abū ʿAmr's reading, he brought the word on its original form. As for the others, they followed the script in that, and since the word is long, lightening it by omission was good, especially on the view of one who claims its verbal status, like al-Fārisī.

Al-Fārisī said: "As for the omission of the alif, it is like «لم يَكُ», «لا أَدْرِ», «أصاب الناسَ جُهْدٌ، ولَوْ تَرَ أهلَ مكة», and [his saying]:

2786 - وصَّانيَ العجَّاجُ فيما وَصَّني ...
(Al-ʿAjjāj charged me with what he charged me...)

in the poetry of Ruʾba," meaning: «لم يكن», «لا أدري», «ولو ترى», and «وصَّاني». Abū ʿUbayd said: "I saw it in the one said to be the Imām, the codex of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: «حاش للَّه» without alif, and the other (occurrence) the same." Al-Kisāʾī related that he saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh likewise. They said: on what Abū ʿUbayd and al-Kisāʾī said, this reading is preferred, and because six of the seven read it. Al-Farrāʾ reported that the full form is the dialect of some Arabs and the omission is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; he said: "Among the Arabs is one who says «حشى زيد», meaning «حشى لزيد»." Al-Farrāʾ reported that the three forms are heard, but the dialect of the Hijaz is preferred in their view.

Al-Aʿmash, with a group, read «حشى للَّه» with both alifs dropped, and it has been mentioned that al-Farrāʾ related it as a dialect of some Arabs, and on it is his saying:

2787 - حشى رَهْطِ النبيِّ. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Except the clan of the Prophet...)

the verse (as above). Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «حاشى اللَّهِ» with the Majestic Name in the genitive, and there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is a noun annexed to the Majestic Name [like «سبحان اللَّه», and this is al-Zamakhsharī's choice. The second: that it is a particle of exception governing the genitive of what follows, and al-Fārisī held this]; and in making «حاشى» a genitive particle meant for exception there is something to consider, since nothing has preceded in the speech from which the Majestic Name would be excepted, unlike «قام القومُ حاشى زيد».

Know that when the grammarians mentioned this particle, they made it among the words that waver between verbal and particle status, according to one who affirmed its verbal status, and made it in that like «خلا» and «عدا», according to one who affirmed the particle status of «عدا». It would have been fitting for them to mention it among those wavering among noun, verb and particle status, as they did with «على», saying that it is a genitive particle in «عليك», a noun in the saying «مِنْ عليه», and a verb in the saying:

2788 - عَلاَ زيدُنا يومَ النَّقا. . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Our Zayd rose up on the day of al-Naqā...)

although there is something to consider in it, which I have given fully elsewhere; its summary is that «على» in its verbal state is other than «على» in its non-verbal state, by the evidence that the alif of the verb is converted from a wāw, and inflection and derivation enter it and not the other two. A defender of al-Fārisī may rely on this and say: if «حاشى» in the majority's reading were a noun, the grammarians would have mentioned that in its wavering between particle and verb; since they did not mention it, it indicates that it is not a noun.

Al-Ḥasan read «حاشْ» with sukūn on the shīn in continuation and pause, as if he treated continuation as pause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from al-Ḥasan that he read «حاشى الإِله», saying: "dropped from «حاشى»," meaning that he read with the last alif dropped, and what the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» stated explicitly indicates it, for he said: "with the alif dropped," then said: "and this indicates that it is a genitive particle governing what follows. As for «الإِله», he disassimilated it, and it is a maṣdar put in the place of the passive participle, its meaning being 'the worshipped,' and the alif of «حاشى» was dropped for lightness."

Al-Shaykh said: "What Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said, that the alif of «حاشى» is dropped in al-Ḥasan's reading, is not definite, unless it is reported from him that he pauses in this reading with sukūn on the shīn; if nothing is reported from him on that, it is possible that the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two sākins, since the original is «حاشى الإِله», then he transferred (the vowel), dropping the hamza and vowelling the lām with its vowel, and did not take this vowelling into account because it is incidental, just as it is dropped in «يَخْشى الإِله», and had he taken the vowel into account, the alif would not have been dropped."

I say: the apparent view is that al-Ḥasan pauses in this reading with sukūn on the shīn, and it is supported by the fact that he put sukūn on the shīn in the other transmission from him; so when something that admits interpretation is brought, it should be taken on what is stated explicitly. And the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ»'s saying "this indicates that it is a genitive particle governing what follows" is not sound, because of what was said that had it been a genitive particle it would be used for exception and nothing precedes from which to except by its genitive noun.

Know that the lām entering the Majestic Name is attached to an omitted element by way of explanation, as it is in «سقياً لك ورعياً لزيد», according to the majority; as for al-Mubarrad and al-Fārisī, it is attached to «حاشى» itself because it is an explicit verb for them both; and it has been mentioned that some claimed it to be redundant.

His saying: {مَا هذا بَشَراً}: the majority apply «ما» as working, in the Hijazi dialect, which is the purest dialect; the dialect of Tamīm is non-operation. The verification of this has been given at the beginning of al-Baqara, together with what I recited about it, namely his saying:

2789 - وأنا النذيرُ بحَرَّةٍ مُسْوَدَّةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I am the warner of a black lava-field...)

the two verses. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported that no one read except in the Hijazi dialect. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever read according to his natural speech of the Banū Tamīm read «بشرٌ» in the nominative, and this is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's claim that it was not read so is not granted.

The majority read «بَشَراً» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, as one word. Al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith al-Ḥanafī read «بشرى» with kasra on the bāʾ, the bāʾ being the preposition entering on «شِرى», so they are two words, a preposition and its genitive noun, and there are interpretations of it. The first: "this is not something bought," putting the maṣdar in the place of the direct object, like «ضَرْب الأمير» ("the Emir's striking"). The second: "this is not something sold," which is also a maṣdar in the place of the direct object, except that the meaning differs. The third: "this is not for a price," meaning that he is too exalted for any of these things to be done to him.

ʿAbd al-Wārith related from Abū ʿAmr, like the reading of al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith, except that he read from him «إلا مَلِك» with kasra on the lām, the singular of «الملوك»; they denied him the lowliness of slaves and affirmed for him the honour of kings.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned the kasra on the lām from al-Ḥasan and Abū l-Ḥuwayrith. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "On this «مَلِك» was read with kasra on the lām," as if he understood that whoever read with kasra on the bāʾ read with kasra on the lām too, for the harmony between the two meanings. Al-Zamakhsharī did not mention this reading with kasra on the bāʾ at all; rather it is understood from his words that he did not come across it, for he said: "It was read «ما هذا بشرى», that is, 'he is not a slave owned and base; this is only a noble angel.' You say «هذا بشرى», that is, 'obtained through purchase,' meaning bought; and you say «هذا لك بشرى أم بِكِرا؟». But the reading (of the majority) is the better, for its agreement with the codex and the correspondence of «بشر» to «ملك»."

His saying "for its agreement with the codex" means that the script is «بشراً» with alif, not with yāʾ, and had the meaning been «بشرى» it would have been written with yāʾ. And his saying "and the correspondence" is evidence that he did not come across the kasra on the lām from one who read with kasra on the bāʾ.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فذلكن} is a mubtadaʾ and the relative is its khabar. She pointed to him with the pointing used for the distant, although he was present, to magnify him and exalt him, so as to show her excuse in her infatuation.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that «ذلك» may be a pointing to the love of Yūsuf, with the pronoun in «فيه» returning to the love, so that «ذلك» would be a pointing to something absent in its proper sense. I say: by "absent" he means "distant"; otherwise pointing is only ever to something present, in general.

His saying: {مَآ آمُرُهُ}: there are two aspects in «ما». The first: that it is a maṣdar particle. The second: that it is a relative, and it is the direct object of «يفعلْ». The hāʾ in «آمُرُه» admits two aspects. The first: return to the relative «ما» when we make it mean "that which." The second: return to Yūsuf. Al-Zamakhsharī did not allow its return to Yūsuf unless «ما» is made a maṣdar, for he said: "If you say: does the pronoun in «آمُره» return to the relative or to Yūsuf? I say: rather to the relative, and the meaning is «ما آمُرُ به», the preposition having been omitted, as in his saying:

2790 - أَمَرْتُكَ الخيرَ. . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I commanded you the good...)

and it is possible to make «ما» a maṣdar particle, so that it returns to Yūsuf, its meaning being: 'and if he does not do my command to him,' that is, what my command requires and entails." I say: on this the first object is omitted, its implied form being «ما آمُره به», and it is the pronoun of Yūsuf.

And the sīn in «استعصم» has two aspects, the first being that it is not on its regular sense of seeking, but that «استفعل» here has the meaning of «افتعل», so «استعصم» and «اعتصم» are one. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الاستعصام» is a form of intensification that indicates thorough refusal and strong self-guarding, as if he were in a state of protection and striving to increase from it; like «استمسك», «استوسع الفَتْقُ», «استجمع الرأيَ» and «استفحل الخطبُ»." So he returned the sīn to its regular sense of seeking, which is a good meaning; for this reason Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He sought protection, held fast to it, and disobeyed me."

Al-Shaykh said: "What the morphologists mentioned about «استعصم» is that it corresponds to «اعتصم», so «استفعل» in it corresponds to «افتعل», and this is better than making «استفعل» in it for seeking, because «اعتصم» indicates the existence of his taking protection, whereas seeking protection does not indicate its attainment. As for its being a form of intensification indicating striving to increase protection, the morphologists did not mention this meaning for «استفعل». As for «استمسك», «استوسع» and «استجمع الرأيَ», «استفعل» in them corresponds to «افتعل», the meaning being «امتسك», «اتَّسع» and «اجتمع». As for «استفحل الخطبُ», «استفعل» in it corresponds to «تفعَّل», that is, «تَفَحَّل الخطب», like «استكبر» and «تكبَّر»."

The majority read «وليَكونَنْ» with the nūn lightened, and they pause on it with alif, treating it like tanwīn; for this reason they drop it after ḍamma or kasra, as «هل تقومون» and «هل تقومين» for «هل تَقُومُن» and «هل تقومِن»; and the nūn that appears in pause is the nūn of the nominative, which they restored when what required its omission is absent; I have set this out earlier.

A group read it with the nūn doubled, which diverges from the script of the codex, as it is written with an alif in it, because pause on it is thus, as in his saying:

2791 - وإياكَ والمَيْتاتِ لا تَقْرَبَنَّها ... ولا تَعْبُدِ الشيطانَ واللَّهَ فاعبدا
(Beware of carrion, do not go near it, and do not worship Satan; worship Allah!)

that is, «فاعبدَنْ», so he turned it into alif, and this is one of the views on the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2792 - قِفا نَبْكِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Halt, you two, let us weep...)

and he treated continuation as pause.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رَبِّ السجن}: the majority read with kasra on the bāʾ because it is annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker, with the kasra sufficing in place of it, which is the purest usage. And «السجن» with kasra on the sīn and nominative nūn, as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar «أحبُّ». «السِّجْن» is detention, and the meaning is: entering the prison.

Some of them read «رَبُّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and genitive nūn, on the basis that «ربُّ» is a mubtadaʾ and «السجنِ» is genitive by annexation, and «أحبُّ» is its khabar, the meaning being: "meeting the keeper of the prison and suffering at his hands is dearer to me."

ʿUthmān and his client Ṭāriq, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Zuhrī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Hurmuz and Yaʿqūb read with fatḥa on the sīn, and the rest like the majority. «السَّجْن» is a maṣdar, that is, "confinement is dearer to me," and «إليَّ» is attached to «أحبُّ». It has already been mentioned that the agent here is governed by «إلى» and the object by lām. In reality, «أَفْعَل» here is not of the elative in its proper sense, because he never loved what they called him to; rather these are two evils and he preferred one of the two evils to the other.

His saying: {أَصْبُ}: the majority read with the bāʾ lightened, from «صَبا يَصْبو», that is, "his longing grew tender." «الصَّبْوة» is inclination toward desire, and from it comes «الصَّبا» (the east wind), because souls incline (taṣbū) to it for the sweetness of its breeze and its comfort. One says «صَبَا يَصْبُو صَباءً وصُبُوَّاً» and «صَبِيَ يصبى صَبَاً», and «الصِّبا» with kasra is diversion and play.

A group read «أَصَبُّ» with the bāʾ doubled, from «صَبَبْتُ صَبابة» ("I was ardent in love"), so I am «صَبٌّ». And «الصَّبابَة» is tenderness of longing and its excess, as if, from the excess of his love, he pours (yanṣabbu) toward what he desires as water pours.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ بَدَا}: there are four aspects about its agent. The best of them: that it is a pronoun returning to «السَّجن» with fatḥa on the sīn, that is, "the imprisoning of him appeared to them," and the word «السِّجن» in the majority's reading indicates this, by implication, and the word «السَّجن» in the reading of one who put fatḥa on the sīn. The second: that the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar understood from the verb «بدا», that is, «بَدا لهم بداءٌ» ("a change of mind appeared to them"), and the poet stated it explicitly in his saying:

2793 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بَدا لك في تلك القَلوص بداءُ
(... a change of mind about that young she-camel occurred to you.)

The third: that the agent is an implied element which the context indicates, that is, "an opinion appeared to them." The fourth: that the sentence «لَيَسْجُنُنَّه» itself is the agent, and this is among the principles of the Kufans.

And «حتى» marks the limit of what precedes it. His saying «لَيَسْجُنُنَّه», on the view of the majority, is the answer to an omitted oath, and that oath and its answer are governed by an implied saying, and that implied saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "such and such appeared to them, as they said: By Allah, they will imprison him for a time."

Al-Ḥasan read «لَتَسْجُنُنَّه» with the tāʾ of the second person, and there are two interpretations in it. The first: that they addressed one another with that. The second: that al-ʿAzīz was addressed with it, as a magnifying of him.

Ibn Masʿūd read «عتى», turning the ḥāʾ of «حتى» into ʿayn, and he taught it to others, and that reached ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who wrote to him: "This Qurʾān was revealed in the dialect of Quraysh, so teach people in their dialect." I say: the substitution of ʿayn for ḥāʾ is a Hudhalī dialect.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ} is resumptive, with no position, and it cannot be a ḥāl, because the two did not say that at the time of entering; nor can it be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because entering does not lead to the dream. And «إني» and what is within its scope are in the position of the accusative, governed by the saying.

And «أراني» here is transitive to two objects, according to some, treating dream-seeing as knowledge-seeing, so the sentence of His saying «أَعْصِرُ» is in the position of the second object; and for one who disallows that, it is in the position of ḥāl for him. Dream-seeing was also treated like knowledge-seeing in the identity of its agent and object as two attached pronouns, and from this is the noble verse; for the agent and the object are identical in meaning, since both refer to the speaker, and they are two attached pronouns. Similar is «رَأَيْتُك في المنام قائماً» ("I saw you in the dream standing") and «زيدٌ رآه قائماً» ("Zayd saw himself standing"), and that is not permissible apart from what is mentioned; you do not say «أَكْرَمْتُني», nor «أكرمْتُك», nor «زيد أكرمه»; if you intend that, say «أكرمتُ نفسي» or «إياي ونفسك», or «إياك ونفسَه», or «إياه». The verification of this has been given before.

When the hamza of transfer enters this dream-verb, it becomes transitive to a third, and this has been given in His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ الله فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلاً} [al-Anfāl: 43], "and had He shown you them as many."

«الخَمْر» is grapes; it is called that metaphorically, because it comes to be that, as one thing is named by another in view of what it was, as in His saying: {وَآتُواْ اليتامى} [al-Nisāʾ: 2] ("and give the orphans [their property]"); and the metaphor of this one is nearer. It was said: rather «الخمر» is grape in reality in the dialect of Ghassān and Azd ʿUmān. From al-Muʿtamir: "I met a Bedouin carrying grapes in a vessel and said: what are you carrying? He said: «خمراً»."

The reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh, «أَعْصِر عنباً», does not indicate synonymy, since it intends explanation and not recitation, as in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh «فوق رأسي ثريداً», for he intended only explanation.

And «تأكل الطير» is an adjective of «خبزاً». «فوق» may be an adverbial of the carrying and may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «خبزاً», because in origin it is an adjective of it. As for the pronoun in His saying «نَبِّئْنا بتأويله», al-Shaykh said: "It returns to what they narrated to him, treated like a demonstrative noun, as if it were said «بتأويل ذلك»." Al-Zamakhsharī preceded him in this, and he made it a question and answer. Another said: "He made the pronoun singular only because each of them asked about his own dream, so it is as if each of them said: tell us the interpretation of what I saw."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
And «تُرْزَقانه» is an adjective of «طعام». His saying «إلا نَبَّأْتُكما» is an exception from a void (istithnāʾ mufarragh). For the sentence after it there are two aspects. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and this is allowed from an indefinite because of its being specified by the description. The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a second adjective of «طعام», the implied form being: "no food provided to you will come to you except while it informs of its interpretation, or while it is informed of its interpretation." And «قبل» is apparently an adverbial of «نَبَّأْتكما», and it may be attached to «تأويله», that is, "I informed you of its interpretation, which occurs before its coming."

His saying: {إِنِّي تَرَكْتُ}: this may be resumptive, by which he informs about himself. It may be an explanation for His saying {ذلكما مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي ربي}, that is, "my abandonment of the worship of other than Allah is a cause of His teaching me that"; and on both aspects it has no grammatical position. And «لا يؤمنون» is an adjective of «قوم». He repeated «هم» in His saying {وَهُمْ بالآخرة هُمْ كَافِرُونَ}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "To indicate that they in particular are disbelievers in the Hereafter, and that others are believers in it." Al-Shaykh said: "«هم», in our view, does not indicate particularity." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not say that «هم» indicates particularity; he said only "the repetition of «هم» is to indicate", so it is the repetition that gives the particularity, and it is a good meaning, which the people of rhetoric (ahl al-bayān) understood.

semin-durr:38-38.t: The Kufans gave sukūn to the yāʾ of «آبائي», and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. And «إبراهيم» and what follows it are a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative as praise.

semin-durr:1-1.t: Discussion of the like of His saying «تلك آياتُ» has already been given at the beginning of Yūnus.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُرْآناً}: three analyses are permitted in it. One: it is a badal from the pronoun of «أَنْزَلْناه», or a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) from it, and the pronoun in «أَنْزَلْناه» on these two views refers to «الكتاب». It was also said: «قُرْآناً» is a direct object and the pronoun in «أَنْزلْناه» is the pronoun of the maṣdar.
«عربيَّاً» is an adjective of the Qur'an. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قُرْآناً» if it carries a pronoun, meaning if we make it a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word, that is, "We sent it down gathered, while being Arabic." Al-ʿarabī is attributed to the Arabs because it was sent down in their language. The singular of al-ʿarab is ʿarabī, as the singular of al-Rūm is Rūmī. ʿArabah, with fatḥa on the rāʾ, is the region of the abode of Ismāʿīl the Prophet, peace be upon him. The poet said:
2377 - وعَرْبَةُ أرضٌ ما يُحِلُّ حرامَها ... مِنَ الناسِ إلا اللَّوْذَعِيُّ الحُلاحِلُ
(ʿArbah is a land whose sanctity none of the people violates but the sharp, noble chief.)
He put sukūn on its rāʾ by necessity; so al-ʿarabī may be attributed to this locale.
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as 2377 in the source, where the sequence suggests 2733; it is reproduced as written.]

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَحْسَنَ القصص}: in the accusative of «أحسنَ» there are two analyses. [One]: that it is accusative as a direct object, but only if you make al-qaṣaṣ a maṣdar standing in the place of the object, like al-khalq in the sense of "the created," or you make it faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl like al-qabaḍ and al-naqaṣ in the sense of "the seized" and "the diminished," that is, "We relate to you the best of the things related." Two: that it is accusative as a clarifying maṣdar (maṣdar mubayyin), if you make al-qaṣaṣ a maṣdar not intended as the object, and the thing related is then omitted, that is, "We relate to you the best relating." «أَحْسَنَ» may be an elative (afʿal tafḍīl) in its basic sense, or may be a mere description by beauty, belonging to the chapter of annexing the attribute to what it describes, that is, "the beautiful narrative."
His saying: {بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: the bāʾ is causal and is attached to «نَقُصُّ», and «ما» is a maṣdar particle, that is, "because of Our revealing."
His saying: {هذا القرآن}: two analyses are permitted in it. One, which is the apparent: it is accusative as the direct object of «أَوْحَيْنا». Two: the matter belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ, I mean between «نَقُصُّ» and «أَوْحَيْنا», for each of them seeks «هذا القرآن», and the matter is one of the second operator acting. This arises only if we make «أَحْسَنَ» accusative as a maṣdar and do not supply an omitted object for «نَقُصُّ».
His saying: «وَإِن كُنتَ» to the end: its like has preceded it.
[Translator's note: the source has a stray slash after «يكونَ» in the first line, a page-break mark, not translated.]

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَ}: regarding its operator there are several analyses, the most apparent being that it is accusative by {قَالَ يابني} [Yūsuf: 5], that is, "Yaʿqūb said: 'O my little son,' at the time of Yūsuf's saying to him such and such." This is the easiest of the analyses, since in it «إذ» remains an adverbial of past time. It was also said: its governor is «الغافلين»; so said Makkī. It was also said: it is accusative by «نَقُصُّ», that is, "We relate to you the time of his saying such and such," and in this «إذ» is taken out of the past and out of being an adverbial; and if you supply the object as omitted, that is, "We relate to you the state at the time of his saying," it must be taken out of the past. It was also said: it is accusative by an implied verb, that is, "remember." It was also said: it is accusative as a badal from «أَحْسَنَ القصص», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because the time includes the narrative, which is the thing related."
His saying: {ياأبت}: Ibn ʿĀmir read with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and the others with kasra. This tāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ of the first person, which is why the two cannot be combined except by necessity, and this is specific to two expressions: yā abat and yā amat. It is not permitted in other nouns; if you said «يا صاحِبَتِ» it would not be permitted at all, just as the words "mother" and "paternal uncle" are specific to a ruling in a case like «يا بن أُمّ». The combination of this tāʾ with either the yāʾ or the alif is permitted by necessity, as in his saying:
2734 - يا أَبَتا عَلَّكَ أو عَساكا
(O my father, perhaps you, or may it be you...)
and the saying of another:
2735 - أيا أَبَتا لا تَزَلْ عندَنا ... فإنَّا نخافُ بأنْ نُخْتَرَمْ
(O my father, do not leave us, for we fear we shall be cut off.)
and the saying of another:
2736 - أيا أبتي لا زِلْتَ فينا فإنَّما ... لنا أَمَلٌ في العيشِ ما دُمْتَ عائِشا
(O my father, may you never cease to be among us, for we have hope in life as long as you live.)
Al-Zamakhsharī's statement suggests that combining the tāʾ and the alif is not by necessity, for he said: "If you ask: what is this kasra? I say: it is the kasra that was before the yāʾ in your saying «يا أبي», and was moved back to the tāʾ because the feminine tāʾ requires that what precedes it be with fatḥa. If you ask: why did the kasra not drop in favour of the fatḥa that the tāʾ requires, leaving the tāʾ sākin? I say: that is impossible in it because it is a noun, and nouns are due to be vowelled because of their originality in case-inflection; sukūn on the yāʾ is allowed, although its basic rule is to be vowelled, for lightening, because it is a soft letter, whereas the tāʾ is a sound letter like the kāf of the pronoun, so it must be vowelled. If you ask: combining this tāʾ with this kasra resembles combining the substitute with what it substitutes for, because it is in the position of the yāʾ when you say «يا غلامِ»; so as «يا أبتي» is not permitted, «يا أبتِ» is not permitted. I say: the yāʾ and the kasra before it are two things, and the tāʾ is a substitute for one of the two things, namely the yāʾ, while the kasra is not addressed; so the substitute and what it substitutes for are not combined, except when the tāʾ and the yāʾ are combined, and nothing else. Do you not see their saying «يا أبتا», where the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ, how combining it with the tāʾ was allowed and was not counted as combining the substitute and what is substituted for? The kasra is more remote than that. If you ask: the kasra in «يا غلامِ» indicated the annexation because it is the companion of the yāʾ and its neighbour; so if it indicates the same in «يا أبت», then the substituted tāʾ is idle, and its existence is like its absence. I say: rather its state with the tāʾ is as its state with the yāʾ when you say «يا أبي»."
Likewise the Shaykh's statement, for he said: "This tāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation, so the two do not combine, but it combines with the alif that is a substitute for the yāʾ. He said:
2737 - يا أَبَتا عَلَّكَ أو عَسَاكا"
There is something to consider in this, in that the alif is like the yāʾ, being a substitute for it, so the two ought not to be combined.
The origin of this tāʾ is for the feminine. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is this tāʾ? I say: a feminine tāʾ that stands as a substitute for the yāʾ of annexation, and the proof that it is a feminine tāʾ is its changing into a hāʾ in pause." I say: what he mentioned about its changing into a hāʾ in pause is how Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read, while the others paused on it with the tāʾ, as if they treated it like the tāʾ of annexation (tāʾ al-ilḥāq) in bint and ukht. Among those who stated explicitly that it is for the feminine is Sībawayh, for he said: "I asked al-Khalīl about the tāʾ in «يا أبت», and he said: 'It is like the tāʾ in khāla and ʿamma,'" meaning that it is for the feminine; and what also indicates that it is for the feminine is their writing it as a hāʾ; and the analogy of one who pauses with the tāʾ is that he write it as a tāʾ, like bint and ukht.
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how is it permissible to attach the feminine tāʾ to a masculine? I say: as it is permitted in your saying «حمامة ذَكَر», «وشاةٌ ذَكَر», «ورجلٌ رَبْعَة», and «وغلام يَفَعَة»." I say: he means that it was brought merely to feminise the word, as in the cited words. Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was it permissible to substitute the feminine tāʾ for the yāʾ of annexation? I say: because the feminine and annexation correspond in that each of them is an addition joined to the noun at its end." I say: this is a remote analogy, not acted upon by the skilled, for it is called the formal resemblance (al-shabah al-ṭardī), meaning a resemblance in form.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يا أَبَت» was read with the three vowels." As for the fatḥa and the kasra, I have attributed them to their readers; as for the ḍamma, it is very strange, and it resembles one who builds the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person on ḍamma, like the reading of one who read, and it will come, Allah willing, {قَالَ رَبُّ احكم} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 112] with ḍamma on the bāʾ; its justification will come there, and why we said that it is annexed to the yāʾ and did not make it a single word without annexation.
The justification of the kasra on this tāʾ has already been given by what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, that it is the kasra before the yāʾ moved back to the tāʾ. This is one of the two doctrines; the other doctrine: it is an extraneous kasra brought to indicate the yāʾ that it replaces; and it is not a disagreement of substance.
As for the fatḥa, it has four analyses, of which al-Fārisī mentioned two. One: that he made do with the fatḥa in place of the alif, meaning the alif converted from the yāʾ, as the other made do with it in place of it in his saying:
2738 - ولَسْتُ براجعٍ ما فاتَ منِّي ... بلَهْفَ ولا بلَيْتَ ولا لَوَنِّي
(I shall not retrieve what has passed me by with "alas" or "would that" or "if only I...")
and as it is made do with in place of it in «يا بن أمَّ» and «يا بنَ عمَّ», as given earlier. Two: that it was shortened (tarkhīm) by dropping the tāʾ, and then the tāʾ was inserted with fatḥa; this is as al-Nābigha said:
2739 - كِليْني لِهَمٍّ يا أُمَيمَةَ ناصِبِ ... وليلٍ أقاسِيه بطيءِ الكواكبِ
(Leave me to a toilsome care, O Umayma, and to a night I endure, slow in its stars.)
with fatḥa on the tāʾ of «أُمَيْمة», as I have mentioned to you.
Three: what al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Ḥātim and Quṭrub in one of his two statements mentioned, namely that the alif in «يا أبتا» is the alif of lamentation (nudba), which he then dropped, making do with the fatḥa in its place. This may help in answering the objection about combining the substitute and what is substituted for. Some have rejected this doctrine, saying that the place is not a place of lamentation.
Four: that the origin is «يا أبةً» with tanwīn, and the tanwīn was dropped because the vocative is a chapter of omission; Quṭrub held this in his second statement. This has been rejected on the ground that the tanwīn is not dropped from the accusative vocative, as in «يا ضارباً رجلاً».
Abū Jaʿfar read «يا أبي» with the yāʾ, not substituting the tāʾ for it.
Al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read: «أحدَ عْشر» with sukūn on the ʿayn, as if they intended by this lightening to alert that the two words are made one word.
His saying: {والشمس والقمر}: two analyses are permitted. One: the wāw is conjunctive, and it may then be of the chapter of mentioning the specific after the general by way of detail, because the sun and the moon entered into His saying {أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً}; so it is like His saying {وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98] after His saying «وملائكتِه». It may also not be so, the wāw being for conjoining something different, so that he saw the sun and the moon in addition to the eleven, unlike the first, in which he saw the eleven, and among them the sun and the moon. Both possibilities are transmitted from the exegetes, and among those who transmitted them is al-Zamakhsharī.
The second analysis: the wāw is the wāw of accompaniment (maʿa). But it is the weaker, because whenever conjunction is possible without weakness or damage to the meaning, it is preferred to accompaniment; and on this it is like the analysis before it, in the sense that he saw the sun and the moon in addition to the eleven stars.
His saying: {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ}: this admits two analyses. One: it is a sentence repeated for emphasis when the separation by objects grew long, so it was repeated, as «أنكم» was repeated in His saying {أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتٌّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُّخْرَجُونَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 35]; so said the Shaykh, and the verification of this will come, Allah the Exalted willing. Two: it is not an emphasis, and al-Zamakhsharī leaned to this, for he said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of repeating «رأيتُهم»? I say: it is not a repetition; it is a resumptive speech on the supposition of a question, being an answer to it, as if Yaʿqūb, peace be upon him, had said to him at His saying {إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً والشمس والقمر}: 'How did you see them?', asking about the state of seeing them, so he said: 'I saw them prostrating to me.'"
I say: this is the more apparent, because whenever the speech revolves between taking it as emphasis or as establishing something new, taking it as the second is preferable.
«ساجدين» is an adjective pluralised with the plural of rational beings. It was said: because he treated them as rational beings in attributing their action to them, he pluralised them with their plural; and a thing may be treated as another thing if it shares in some attribute.
The seeing here is a seeing in a dream, and it has already been given that it governs two objects, like the seeing of knowing; and on this the second object of {رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً} would have been omitted, but omitting it by abbreviation only (iqtiṣār) is impossible, so only omission by condensation (ikhtiṣār) remains, which is rare or impossible according to some.
[Translator's note: the source has stray slashes at "ذكرْتُها ... /" and "أَنَّكُمْ / إِذَا", which are page-break marks, not translated. In the third paragraph of Quṭrub's analyses, the source prints «با أبتا» with bāʾ, evidently for «يا أبتا»; it is translated as «يا أبتا».]

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ وَالْفَحْشَاءَ إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى): the answer of «لَوْلَا» is omitted, its implied form being "لَهَمَّ بِهَا" ("he would have inclined to her"); on this view the pause is at وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ. The meaning is that he did not incline to her.
It is also said: the implied form is "had he not seen the proof, he would have committed the sin".
(كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), i.e. "the matter is thus" (الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِكَ).
It is also said: in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. "a seeing like that" (رُؤْيَةٌ كَذَلِكَ).
The lām in «لِنَصْرِفَ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted element.
And (الْمُخْلَصِينَ) is read with kasra on the lām, i.e. "those who make their deeds sincere" (الْمُخْلِصِينَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ); and with fatḥa on it, i.e. "those whom Allah has made pure for His obedience".

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى الْبَابِ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءًا إِلَّا أَنْ يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ دُبُرٍ): the majority read it with the genitive and tanwīn.
Among the irregular (shādhdh) readings it was read with three ḍammas and without tanwīn (مِنْ دُبُرُ); it is then indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it has been cut off from the genitive construct (iḍāfa). The original is "مِنْ دُبُرِهِ" and "قُبُلِهِ", and then what was done with قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ was done with it. This is weak, because the genitive construct is not necessary to it in the way that it is necessary to the adverbs (ẓurūf) that become indeclinable when cut off from the genitive construct.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا وَاسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنْبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنْتِ مِنَ الْخَاطِئِينَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the implied form is "يَا يُوسُفُ" ("O Yūsuf").
Al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa; the more likely explanation is that he brought it out according to the original form of the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), as came in poetry:
يَا عَدِيًّا لَقَدْ وَقَتْكَ الْأَوَاقِي
("O ʿAdī, the protectors have indeed protected you")
It is also said: this reading was not accurately recorded from al-Aʿmash, and the more likely explanation is that he paused on the word and then joined it, treating the joining like the pause; so he threw the vowel of the hamza onto the fāʾ and dropped the hamza, and the word came to be pronounced (يُوسُفَ اعْرِضْ). This is like what has been reported: «اللَّهُ أَكْبَرَ اشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا. . .» — with joining and fatḥa.
Among the irregular readings it was also read with ḍamma on the fāʾ and with أَعْرَضَ in the form of the past verb; this is weak because of His saying «وَاسْتَغْفِرِي»; it would have been more fitting for it to be with fāʾ: «فَاسْتَغْفِرِي».

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ تُرَاوِدُ فَتَاهَا عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا إِنَّا لَنَرَاهَا فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِسْوَةٌ): it is read with kasra on the nūn and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms.
The alif of «الْفَتَى» is converted from a yāʾ, because they say فَتَيَانِ; and الْفُتُوَّةُ is irregular (shādhdh).
(قَدْ شَغَفَهَا): it is read with ghayn, and it is from shaghāf al-qalb, which is the heart's covering (membrane). The meaning is that it reached the membrane of her heart, and that love of him came to enclose her heart as the membrane encloses it.
It is also read with ʿayn (شَعَفَهَا); it is from your saying "فُلَانٌ مَشْعُوفٌ بِكَذَا", i.e. "infatuated with it and passionately devoted to it".
And (حُبًّا) is a tamyīz (specification); the original is "قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبُّهُ" ("his love has smitten her"). The clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تُرَاوِدُ» or from «الْفَتَى».

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً وَآتَتْ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُ أَكْبَرْنَهُ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَعْتَدَتْ): it is from al-ʿatād, which is the thing made ready for a matter.
(مُتَّكَأً): the majority read it with doubling (tashdīd) of the tāʾ and with hamza, without lengthening (madd). The original of the word is مُوتَكَأً, from تَوَكَّأْتُ ("I leaned"), and what is meant by it is the sitting place in which one reclines; the wāw was replaced by a tāʾ and assimilated.
It was read irregularly with lengthening and hamza (مُتَّكَاءً), the alif in it arising from the prolongation (ishbāʿ) of the fatḥa.
It is also read with tanwīn without hamza (مُتَّكًا); the explanation of it is that he replaced the hamza with an alif and then dropped it because of the tanwīn.
Ibn Jinnī said: it may be from أَوْكَيْتُ السِّقَاءَ ("I tied up the waterskin"); the alif would then be a replacement for the yāʾ, and its pattern would be mufta'al from that.
It is also read with the tāʾ undoubled and without hamza (مُتْكًا); and it is said: al-mutk is the citron (al-utrujj).
(حَاشَى لِلَّهِ): it is read with two alifs, and that is the original.
The majority hold that it is a verb here; they have said from it أُحَاشِي ("I except"); and this is supported by the entry of the lām on the name of Allah the Exalted: if it were a preposition, it would not enter upon a preposition. Its agent (fāʿil) is implied (muḍmar), its implied form being "حَاشَى يُوسُفُ", i.e. "Yūsuf kept far from sin out of fear of Allah".
The origin of the word is from حَاشَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ; so حَاشَى means "he went to a ḥāshiya", i.e. to one side.
It is also read without an alif after the shīn (حَاشَ); it was dropped for lightness, and in that the Muṣḥaf was followed; what made this acceptable is the frequency of its use.
It was read irregularly «حَشَا لِلَّهِ», without an alif after the ḥāʾ; it is a lightened form of it.
Some of them said: it is a preposition and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); this is weak, because the place for something like this is poetic necessity.
(مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا): it is read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "a human being"; rather, he is an angel.
It is also read with kasra on the bāʾ (بِشِرًى), from al-shirāʾ ("buying"), i.e. "this was not obtained for a price". It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the passive participle (mafʿūl), i.e. "something bought"; and on this view «مَلِكٌ» was read with kasra on the lām ("a king").

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَبِّ السِّجْنُ): it is read with kasra on the sīn and ḍamma on the nūn; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَحَبُّ» is its khabar (predicate). What is meant is the place of confinement, and the implied form is "living in the prison".
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn (السَّجْنُ), as a maṣdar (verbal noun: "imprisonment").
It is also read «رَبُّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, without yāʾ, «وَالسِّجْنِ» with kasra on the sīn and the genitive by genitive construct, i.e. "the master of the prison"; and the implied form is "meeting him" or "enduring him".

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الْآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّى حِينٍ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَدَا لَهُمْ): concerning the agent (fāʿil) of «بَدَا» there are three views. The first: it is omitted, and (لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ) stands in its place, i.e. "imprisonment appeared (fitting) to them"; it was omitted and the clause was put in its place; but the clause is not the agent, because clauses cannot be such. The second: the agent is implied (muḍmar), and it is the maṣdar of بَدَا, i.e. "an appearing (بَدَاءٌ) appeared to them", and it was left implied. The third: the agent is what the speech points to, i.e. "an opinion appeared to them" (بَدَا لَهُمْ رَأْيٌ), and it too was left implied. And (حَتَّى) is attached to «يَسْجُنُنَّهُ». And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ): the majority read it with kasra on the sīn, and it was read with fatḥa on it (السَّجْنَ); the implied form is "the place of imprisonment" or "into the prison".
And (قَالَ) is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), because he did not tell that dream at the time of his entering; nor is it an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because entering does not lead to the dream.
(فَوْقَ رَأْسِي): an adverb (ẓarf) of «أَحْمِلُ».
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْخُبْز». And «تَأْكُلُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:39-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (٣٩) مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٤٠) يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ): «أَمْ» here is the connected (muttaṣila) one.
(سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا): it takes two objects, and the second has been omitted, i.e. "you named them gods".
And «أَسْمَاءً» here means "things named", or "possessors of names", because a name is not worshipped.
(أَمَرَ أَلَّا): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) with (قَدْ) intended along with it; but this is weak because of the weakness of what governs it.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُمَا): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «نَاجٍ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِي»; it is not attached to «نَاجٍ», because the meaning is not according to that.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَرَى سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُؤْيَايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ (٤٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (سِمَانٍ): an adjective (ṣifa) of «بَقَرَاتٍ». In (ordinary) speech it would be permissible to put it in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «سَبْعَ».
And (يَأْكُلُهُنَّ) is in the position of the genitive or the accusative, according to what we have mentioned. Likewise «خُضْرٍ».
(لِلرُّؤْيَا): the lām in it is redundant (zāʾida), strengthening the verb since its object has been put before it; it may be dropped outside the Qurʾān, because one says عَبَّرْتُ الرُّؤْيَا ("I interpreted the dream").

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ): i.e. "these are…".
(بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ): i.e. "the interpretation of the jumbles of dreams (أَضْغَاثِ الْأَحْلَامِ)"; this is necessary, because they did not claim ignorance of interpreting dreams.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَجَا مِنْهُمَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun; it is not a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It may also be a ḥāl from «الَّذِي».
And (ادَّكَرَ): its original is اذْتَكَرَ; the dhāl was replaced by a dāl and the tāʾ by a dāl, and the first was assimilated into the second, so that the two letters come close.
It is read irregularly with a doubled dotted dhāl (اذَّكَرَ); its explanation is that he changed the tāʾ into a dhāl and assimilated.
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ): it is read with ḍamma on the hamza and with kasra on it, i.e. "a favour", namely his release from prison; it may also mean "a period of time".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza and the mīm and a hāʾ with tanwīn (أَمَهٍ); this is forgetfulness; one says: أَمِهَ يَأْمَهُ أَمَهًا.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دَأَبًا): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you will toil persistently" (تَدْأَبُونَ); the speech points to it.
It is read with sukūn on the hamza and with fatḥa on it; the verb from it is دَأَبَ دَأْبًا and دَئِبَ دَأْبًا.
It is also read with an alif without hamza, by lightening (takhfīf).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَعْصِرُونَ): it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ and with fatḥa; the object is omitted, i.e. "they press grapes", because of the abundance of fertility.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the ṣād (تُعْصَرُونَ), i.e. "you will be rained upon"; it is from His saying (مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ).

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ الْآنَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ): what governs the adverb (ẓarf) is «خَطْبُكُنَّ»; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) by which a grave matter has been named, and it governs by virtue of its meaning, because its meaning is "what did you intend?" or "what did you do?".

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ): i.e. "the matter is that"; and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "Allah made that manifest so that he may know".

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي): concerning «مَا» there are two views:
The first: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and its position is the accusative; the implied form is "the soul is indeed ever commanding evil, except at the time of my Lord's mercy". Its parallel is (وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا), whose being in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) they have mentioned; it is like your saying "I did not stand except on Friday". The other view: that «مَا» means «مَنْ» ("whoever"); the implied form is "the soul commands evil, except for the one on whom my Lord has mercy", or "except a soul on which my Lord has mercy, for it does not command evil".

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ): «حَيْثُ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَتَبَوَّأُ». It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مِنْهَا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَتَبَوَّأُ»; it may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حَيْثُ», because «حَيْثُ» is not complete except with the muḍāf ilayhi, and putting the ḥāl before the muḍāf ilayhi is not permissible.
And (يَشَاءُ) with yāʾ: its agent (fāʿil) is the pronoun of Yūsuf. With nūn (نَشَاءُ): it is the pronoun of the name of Allah, by way of magnification. It may also be that its agent is the pronoun of Yūsuf, because his will is from the will of Allah.
The lām in «لِيُوسُفَ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "We established Yūsuf".
It may also not be redundant, the object being omitted, i.e. "We established matters for Yūsuf".
And (يَتَبَوَّأُ) is a ḥāl from Yūsuf.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ اجْعَلُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِفِتْيَتِهِ): it is read with tāʾ on the pattern fiʿla; it is a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla) like صِبْيَةٌ. And with nūn (لِفِتْيَانِهِ), like غِلْمَانٌ, which is one of the plurals of multitude (jumūʿ al-kathra); on this view it occurs in the place of the plural of paucity.
(إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا): what governs «إِذَا» is «يَعْرِفُونَهَا».

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَكْتَلْ): it is read with nūn, because sending him is a cause of the measuring for the group. And with yāʾ (يَكْتَلْ), on the view that the agent is the brother; since he was the cause, the verb was attributed to him, so it is as if he is the one who measures for the group.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ هَلْ آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ): in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a trusting like my trusting you with his brother".
(خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا): it is read with the alif, and it is a tamyīz (specification); something like this may be put in a genitive construct. It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also read «حِفْظًا», and it is a tamyīz and nothing else.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذَلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رُدَّتْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and that is the original.
It is also read with kasra on it (رِدَّتْ); its explanation is that he transferred the kasra of the second radical (ʿayn) to the first radical (fāʾ), as was done in قِيلَ and بِيعَ; and the doubled verb (muḍāʿaf) resembles the weak verb (muʿtall).
(مَا نَبْغِي): «مَا» is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by «نَبْغِي». It may also be negating; then in (نَبْغِي) there are two views. The first: it means "we seek", so the object is omitted, i.e. "we do not seek wrongdoing". The second: that it is intransitive, meaning "we do not transgress".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّى تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّا آتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ): it is the answer to an oath according to the meaning, because the covenant (al-mīthāq) means an oath.
(إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ): it is an exception from a different genus (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins).
It may also be from the same genus; the implied form would then be "you shall surely bring him to me in every circumstance except in the circumstance of your being surrounded".

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ): concerning the answer of «لَمَّا» there are two views:
The first: it is «آوَى» (in the next verse), and it is the answer of the first «لَمَّا» and of the second, like your saying "when I came to you and when I spoke to you, you answered me". What made this acceptable is that their entering upon Yūsuf follows their entering through the gates.
The second: it is omitted, its implied form being "they complied", or "they fulfilled their father's need", and the like.
It may also be that the answer is the meaning of «مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ».
And (حَاجَةً) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the agent (fāʿil) of «يُغْنِي» is "the dispersal" (التَّفَرُّقُ).

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَى يُوسُفَ آوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ إِنِّي أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ إِنِّي أَنَا): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf); and likewise, everything that requires an answer, whose answer has been mentioned, and after which «قَالَ» then comes — it is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:72-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ (٧٢) قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ (٧٣) قَالُوا فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ (٧٤) قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ (٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and an alif after the wāw.
It is also read without the alif; some of them put ḍamma on the ṣād (صُوعَ) and some put fatḥa on it (صَوْعَ).
It is also read «صَاعَ الْمَلِكِ». All of these are dialectal forms of it, and it is the vessel from which one drinks.
It is also read «صَوْغَ الْمَلِكِ», with a dotted ghayn, i.e. "the thing he had wrought (of metal)".
(قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ): there are three views on it:
The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "its penalty with us is like its penalty with you"; the hāʾ refers back to the thief or to the theft, and the preceding speech gives evidence for both. On this view, His saying (مَنْ وُجِدَ) is a mubtadaʾ, «فَهُوَ» is a second mubtadaʾ, (جَزَاؤُهُ) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first.
And (مَنْ) is conditional, and the fāʾ is its answer.
It may also mean «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), the fāʾ entering into its khabar because of the vagueness in it; the implied form is "the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found — it (i.e. the enslavement) is the penalty of the thief".
It may also be that the hāʾ in «جَزَاؤُهُ» refers to the theft.
The second view: that «جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «مَنْ وُجِدَ» its khabar, the implied form being "the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found"; and «فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar emphasising the meaning of the first.
The third view: that «جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «مَنْ وُجِدَ» a second mubtadaʾ, «فَهُوَ» a third mubtadaʾ, and «جَزَاؤُهُ» the khabar of the third; the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) back to the first mubtadaʾ is the last hāʾ, and back to the second it is «هُوَ».
(كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a recompense like that".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ كَذَلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ): the majority read it with kasra on the wāw, and that is the original, because it is from وَعَى يَعِي ("to contain").
It is also read with hamza (إِعَاءِ), the hamza being a replacement for the wāw; they are two dialectal forms; one says وِعَاءٌ and إِعَاءٌ, وِشَاحٌ and إِشَاحٌ, وِسَادَةٌ and إِسَادَةٌ. They resorted to the hamza only because of the heaviness of the kasra on the wāw.
It is also read with ḍamma on it (وُعَاءِ), and that is a dialectal form.
If it is asked: why did He not say "فَاسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِنْهُ" ("then he took it out of it"), since it had already been mentioned? It is answered: He had not explicitly stated the searching of his brother's bag so as to refer back to it with a pronoun; so He mentioned it overtly, so that this would be a pointer to what is omitted; its implied form is "then he searched his brother's bag and took it out of it".
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ كِدْنَا), (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ) and (دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ): all of this has already been mentioned.
(وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ): it is read irregularly «ذِي عَالِمٍ», and there are three views on it:
The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْبَاطِلُ. The second: «ذِي» is redundant (zāʾida); the like of that has come in poetry, as in the saying of al-Kumayt:
إِلَيْكُمْ ذَوِي آلِ النَّبِيِّ
("To you, O family of the Prophet")
The third: that he put the name in a genitive construct with the thing named, which is omitted, its implied form being "possessor of what is named 'knower'", as in the saying of the poet:
إِلَى الْحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ السَّلَامِ عَلَيْكُمَا
("Until the year is out; then the name of peace be upon you both")

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ قَالَ أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَسَرَّهَا): the pronoun refers back to their attributing theft to him; the speech has pointed to it.
It is also said: there is a fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech, its implied form being "he said within himself: you are worse in position"; and «أَسَرَّهَا», i.e. this statement.
And (مَكَانًا) is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "worse than him" or "than the two of them".

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ): it (مَكَانَهُ) is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «خُذْ».
It may also be construed according to the meaning, i.e. "put one of us in his place".

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ أَنْ نَأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا مَتَاعَنَا عِنْدَهُ إِنَّا إِذًا لَظَالِمُونَ (٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is "from that we should take" (مِنْ أَنْ نَأْخُذَ).

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْأَسُوا مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا نَجِيًّا قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمِنْ قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطْتُمْ فِي يُوسُفَ فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الْأَرْضَ حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أَبِي أَوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ (٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اسْتَيْأَسُوا): it is read with a yāʾ followed by a hamza; it is from يَئِسَ ("to despair").
It is also read اسْتَيْأَسُوا with an alif after the tāʾ and before the yāʾ (اسْتَايَسُوا); it is a metathesised form (maqlūb): one says يَئِسَ and أَيِسَ, and the original is with the yāʾ first, and the inflection of the word follows that. As for «إِيَاسٌ», the name of a man, it is not the maṣdar of this verb; rather it is the maṣdar of أُسْتُهُ, i.e. "I gave him". However, the hamza in the verse was changed into an alif for lightening.
[Translator's note: the source writes the second reading with the same spelling اسْتَيْأَسُوا as the first, while describing it as having an alif after the tāʾ; the form described is اسْتَايَسُوا.]
(نَجِيًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «خَلَصُوا»; it is a singular in the place of a plural, i.e. "confidants" (أَنْجِيَةٌ), as Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا).
And (مِنْ قَبْلُ): i.e. "and before that".
(مَا فَرَّطْتُمْ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it is redundant (zāʾida), and «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, i.e. "and you fell short before". The second: it is maṣdariyya, and concerning its position there are three views. The first: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «مِنْ قَبْلُ» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "and your falling short regarding Yūsuf was before". This is weak, because «قَبْلُ», when it occurs as a khabar or a ṣila, is not cut off from the genitive construct, lest it remain incomplete. The second: its position is accusative, conjoined to what «تَعْلَمُوا» governs; its implied form is "did you not know your father's taking the covenant from you and your falling short regarding Yūsuf?". The third: it is conjoined to the noun of «إِنَّ», its implied form being "and that your falling short before regarding Yūsuf…".
It is also said: it is weak on these two views, because in them there is a separation between the conjunction and the maʿṭūf (conjoined); but we have made clear in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ that this is of no account.
As for the khabar of «إِنَّ» on the last view, it may be «فِي يُوسُفَ», and this is preferable so that «مِنْ قَبْلُ» is not made the khabar.
(فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الْأَرْضَ): it (الْأَرْضَ) is the object of «أَبْرَحَ», i.e. "I will not leave"; it may also be an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ارْجِعُوا إِلَى أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا يَا أَبَانَا إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَا إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَافِظِينَ (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَرَقَ): it is read with fatḥa and without doubling, i.e. "according to what appeared to us".
It is also read with ḍamma on the sīn and doubling of the rāʾ with kasra on it (سُرِّقَ), i.e. "he was accused of theft".

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيهَا وَالْعِيرَ الَّتِي أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ (٨٢)).
